# Create full video playthroughs

## Problem statement

`npm run capture` records a **fixed-length** clip (default 15 s) driven by a
wall-clock scripted key plan, so it can never show a whole run: it starts
mid-menu and stops arbitrarily, long before any victory or defeat screen. We
need the capture routine to record a **complete game from the start of play to
the end of the run** — across however many levels that run spans — and to keep
recording for **5 seconds after the victory or defeat moment**.

## Users

- **Primary — the maintainer / release owner.** Wants a single command that
  produces a full, shareable playthrough video (demo / marketing / release
  evidence) without hand-holding the recorder.
  - *As the maintainer, I run `npm run capture` once and get a video of a
    complete run, from Play Game to 5 s past the victory or defeat screen.*
- **Secondary — future CI / QA.** Wants a repeatable full-run clip as
  regression evidence (the run length varies, so the tooling must detect the
  end rather than assume a duration).
- **Tertiary — the shipped-game player.** Benefits indirectly: the in-game
  demo/attract lifecycle must pause briefly on the game-over screen so an
  onlooker (and the capture) can see the outcome before it loops.

## Existing state

- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` boots Vite + headless Chromium, presses
  Enter, replays a **fixed-duration** plan from `scripts/capture-bot.mjs`
  (`buildScriptedPlan` / `BASE_SWEEP_PATTERN`), records the canvas via
  `canvas.captureStream(60)` + `MediaRecorder`, and probes the clip for
  non-triviality.
- There is **no end-of-run detection**: the recorder stops when the plan's
  hold time elapses (`--duration`, default `DEFAULT_CAPTURE_DURATION_MS =
  15_000`).
- A run ends when the boss dies (victory) or the player runs out of lives
  (defeat): `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` `_finishRun(won)` calls
  `scene.start('GameOverScene', { won, score })`; `src/core/GameState.ts`
  `defeatBoss()` / `playerDied()` set `gameState = 'gameover'`.
- The shipped game exposes **no page-side signal** for that transition — the
  capture only has the canvas.
- The in-game demo/attract mode does **not exist yet**; it is tracked by
  Demo mode engine: input seam and lifecycle in PlayScene
  (AH-0MUX495VG0014MIY) and Capture tooling records the in-game demo
  (AH-0MUX496IJ0041O3V), both currently `blocked`. Per its AC3 the demo
  lifecycle returns to the menu / restarts when a run ends.
- Existing capture harness: `scripts/capture-progress.mjs` (progress/ETA) and
  hermetic tests in `scripts/capture-gameplay.test.ts`.

## Desired change

1. **End-of-run signal (Q1A).** The game emits a small **read-only page-side
   signal** when a run ends — a `CustomEvent` on `window` (e.g.
   `aihell:run-ended` with `{ won, score }`) and/or a
   `window.__aiHellRunState` flag set on the `GameOverScene` transition. It
   must be additive/dev-gated so the shipped bundle and normal play are
   unaffected.
2. **Full-run capture (Q2A).** `npm run capture` records one run from the
   start of play (Play Game / demo entry) through **every level that run
   spans** to the first game over, then keeps recording for a configurable
   **tail of 5 000 ms** after the signal before stopping — for **both** a
   victory and a defeat.
3. **Safety cap.** A `--max-duration` bound (generous default) stops the
   recording if no end-of-run signal arrives, so a stuck run cannot record
   forever; hitting the cap is reported explicitly.
4. **Demo dwell (Q3A).** In demo mode, hold on the game-over screen for a
   configurable dwell (≥ 5 s, i.e. ≥ the capture tail) before returning to
   the menu / restarting, so the captured tail shows the victory/defeat
   screen. Normal (non-demo) play is unchanged.
5. **Backwards compatibility.** The explicit fixed-length mode
   (`--duration`) and the scripted-plan path remain available; only the
   default behaviour for `npm run capture` becomes the full-run capture.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (signal):** A run ending in victory or defeat emits a documented,
  read-only page-side signal (`aihell:run-ended` `CustomEvent` on `window`
  and/or `window.__aiHellRunState`) containing the outcome. The signal is
  additive: normal play and the shipped bundle are unaffected, and it fires
  for **both** outcomes.
- **AC2 (full capture):** `npm run capture` records a complete run from the
  start of play through all levels to the first game over, then continues
  recording for the configurable tail (default 5 000 ms) after the signal,
  and stops. Verified for a victory path and a defeat path.
- **AC3 (safety cap):** A configurable `--max-duration` cap bounds the
  recording; when the cap is hit without an end signal the tool reports it
  clearly and exits non-zero (a capped clip is not silently presented as a
  complete run). `--tail <ms>` configures the post-signal tail.
- **AC4 (demo dwell):** In demo mode the game-over screen dwells for a
  configurable period of at least the capture tail before the demo loops or
  returns to the menu; non-demo play is byte-for-byte unchanged.
- **AC5 (tests):** Hermetic unit tests cover: decoding the end-of-run signal
  payload, the tail/cap calculations, and the demo-dwell decision; an
  integration test asserts that a stubbed end-of-run signal stops the
  recording after the tail. Existing capture tests continue to pass.
- **AC6 (documentation):** `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` and the
  `README.md` capture section document the new default full-run behaviour,
  `--max-duration` / `--tail`, the end-of-run signal, and the demo dwell,
  including code comments for the new signal and constant.
- **AC7 (suite):** Full project test suite (`npm test`), `npm run build` and
  `npm run typecheck` all pass with the new changes. (CHANGELOG is managed by
  the ship skill and is excluded.)

## Constraints

- **Dependency:** blocked by the in-game demo engine
  (AH-0MUX495VG0014MIY) and Capture tooling records the in-game demo
  (AH-0MUX496IJ0041O3V); the run is captured via demo mode.
- **Opt-in tooling:** capture stays outside the shipped bundle; the only
  `src/` addition is the small, additive end-of-run signal (dev-gated) and
  the demo dwell.
- **Testability:** the browser/encode path cannot run under vitest (the
  canvas is stubbed), so all new decision logic (signal decoding, tail/cap,
  dwell) must be pure and unit-tested; the browser path is exercised by
  `npm run capture`.
- **Non-deterministic runs:** the game is not fully deterministic (unseeded
  wave/spawn RNG), so the run length varies and the design must rely on the
  end-of-run signal, never on an assumed duration.
- **Cost:** long runs mean longer wall-clock and larger WebM files; the cap
  and progress heartbeat must make this visible and bounded.
- **Backwards compatibility:** `--duration` (fixed length) and the scripted
  fallback remain functional.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — wait for the end signal, record the tail, enforce the cap; report outcome
- `scripts/capture-bot.mjs` — pure helpers for end-signal decoding / tail+cap logic (co-located with existing pure predicates)
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.test.ts` — unit tests for the new pure helpers
- `scripts/capture-progress.mjs` — progress/heartbeat across an unbounded (capped) recording
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — emit the end-of-run signal in `_finishRun`; demo-mode game-over dwell
- `src/scenes/GameOverScene.ts` — outcome available for the signal (if emitted here instead)
- `src/core/GameState.ts` — `gameover` / `bossDefeated` outcome source
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — document full-run capture, signal, cap, dwell
- `README.md` — update the capture command section

## Related work

- Smart capture bot: survival-first heuristic… (AH-0MUX2NENC008AHOQ) — parent epic (`plan_complete`); this work extends its capture/demo pipeline.
- Capture tooling records the in-game demo (AH-0MUX496IJ0041O3V) — sibling; **blocks** this item (capture must first record the demo).
- Demo mode engine: input seam and lifecycle in PlayScene (AH-0MUX495VG0014MIY) — sibling; **blocks** this item (provides the demo run and the lifecycle to dwell on game over).
- Documentation for attract/demo mode and bot (AH-0MUX4975J0045VDZ) — sibling; capture documentation must stay consistent with it.
- Spike: automated gameplay video capture (AH-0MUWMFF3C002WOBK) — the pipeline this builds on.
- Scripted Gameplay Videos (AH-0MUX2NLFZ00128WC) — related `idea`: multi-scene scripted video (fades between scenes); distinct from a single full-run capture, but shares the capture harness.

### Related work (automated report)

#### Related work items
- **AH-0MTEI0XRD0042ZEZ** – Write AC2+AC3: smooth return and no jump tests (completed)
- **AH-0MUNR5LM1004B223** – Add wave-timeout to all enemy gyms (except boss) (completed)
- **AH-0MUDYTPMC002GLEJ** – Add bullet TTL to enemy configurator (completed)

#### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: adjust, capture, captures, complete, create, ending, full, game, moment, npm, past, present, run, seconds, should, video
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: adjust, capture, complete, create, defeat, ending, full, game, moment, npm, present, run, seconds, should
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: capture, captures, complete, create, ending, full, game, npm, present, run, seconds, should

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the demo engine (AH-0MUX495VG0014MIY) will own the run lifecycle; this item adds only the dwell, coordinated with that item. If the demo engine instead already holds on game over, the dwell becomes a no-op/config.
- **Risk (signal race):** the run could end before the capture attaches its listener. *Mitigation:* install the listener via `page.addInitScript` before the game boots, and read the `window.__aiHellRunState` flag as a fallback.
- **Risk (production signal):** a `window` event in shipped code. *Mitigation:* gate it to the dev/test build (`import.meta.env.DEV`) or make it provably inert, and verify `npm run check-bundle` still passes.
- **Risk (long run):** high wall-clock and large files on a full victory run. *Mitigation:* `--max-duration` cap, visible heartbeat, and documented cost in `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`.
- **Risk (headless stability):** long headless WebGL/MediaRecorder sessions may drop frames or fail. *Mitigation:* probe still gates non-triviality; document the run-time expectation.
- **Assumption:** the tail should show the game-over screen, hence the demo dwell; if the operator later prefers the menu in the tail, the dwell can be removed.
- **Scope-creep risk:** multi-scene scripted videos (AH-0MUX2NLFZ00128WC), MP4 export, and full determinism are **out of scope** — link them as separate work items rather than widening this one.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — How should capture detect the run's end (victory/defeat)?**
  - **Answer (Map, interactive reply):** **A** — add a small read-only page-side signal (a DOM `CustomEvent` / `window.__aiHellRunState`) emitted by the game when a run ends.
  - Options A (page-side signal) / B (expose dev-only game instance) / C (canvas OCR). Recommended A.
- **Q2 — What does "a complete game" mean, and when does recording stop?**
  - **Answer (Map, interactive reply):** **A**, with the clarification that it is **start → 5 seconds after the game ends in victory or defeat**, and the run **may span more than one level** (it is a whole run, not a fixed level). A safety cap is accepted.
  - Options A (one run, win or lose, +5 s tail) / B (victory only, retry on defeat) / C (multiple attract-loop runs). Recommended A.
- **Q3 — Sequencing vs the demo-mode epic, and the 5 s tail.**
  - **Answer (Map, interactive reply):** **A** — sequence this item after the demo-mode epic; the demo holds on the game-over screen for a configurable dwell (≥ 5 s) so the captured tail is meaningful. Record `blocked-by` dependencies on the demo engine and the demo-capture sibling.
  - Options A (sequence after epic + demo dwell) / B (implement now on scripted bot) / C (record demo without changing lifecycle). Recommended A.

No OPEN QUESTIONs remain.


## Plan (2026-10-07)

Decomposed into six child work items (dependency order). The design keeps all
new decision logic pure and browser-free so it is hermetic and unit-tested,
while the shipped-game addition is limited to the additive, dev-gated
end-of-run signal and the demo game-over dwell.

### Child work items (dependency order)

1. **Run-end signal, tail and dwell helpers** (AH-0MUXZ49PY0065K2O) — no
   dependencies. Test-first foundation: the pure contracts for decoding the
   run-ended payload, the tail/cap arithmetic, the cap-hit decision and the
   demo dwell, with unit tests. Parent AC5.
2. **Emit dev-gated end-of-run signal** (AH-0MUXZ4BXK001QCEK) — depends on 1.
   `PlayScene._finishRun` emits `aihell:run-ended` and sets
   `window.__aiHellRunState`, both outcomes, `import.meta.env.DEV`-gated.
   Parent AC1.
3. **Demo-mode game-over dwell** (AH-0MUXZ4CAE008QRFZ) — depends on 1. Demo
   holds on the game-over screen for `DEMO_GAME_OVER_DWELL_MS` (>= tail),
   non-scoring, before returning to the menu. Parent AC4.
4. **Full-run capture wait, tail and cap** (AH-0MUXZ4CNS009RV40) — depends on
   1, 2. Default `npm run capture` waits for the signal (init-script listener
   + flag fallback), records `--tail` (default 5000 ms), enforces
   `--max-duration`, and fails non-zero on a cap hit. Parent AC2/AC3.
5. **Full-run capture integration verification** (AH-0MUXZ4D0M001IWW1) —
   depends on 3, 4. Stubbed-signal integration tests (victory + defeat + cap),
   dwell-vs-tail check, and green `npm test` / `npm run build` /
   `npm run typecheck`. Parent AC5/AC7.
6. **Document full-run capture and dwell** (AH-0MUXZ4DDV0098ZW4) — depends on
   2, 3, 4. `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` and `README.md`. Parent AC6.

### Vertical slice phasing

Each child is an end-to-end increment (code + tests where applicable):
pure contracts → in-game signal → demo dwell → capture loop → integration
verification → documentation. Between phases, review and update the next
child's description before starting it.

### Test-first ordering

Child 1 lands the pure-function contracts and their failing/passing unit
tests before the wiring children consume them. Children 3 and 4 add their own
unit tests; child 5 provides the stubbed end-to-end integration verification.

### Plan-run clarifications

No new interview questions were required: the intake Appendix (Q1-Q3) already
answers the end-of-run detection, the meaning of "complete run" and the
sequencing vs the demo epic. Two **implementation** choices remain for the
producer, each with a recommended option (recorded as OPEN QUESTIONs, not
blocking):

- **OPEN QUESTION (dwell mechanism):** the demo engine (AH-0MUX495VG0014MIY)
  currently **skips `GameOverScene`** on game over for its non-scoring rule, so
  AC4 ("the game-over screen dwells...") needs a demo-safe game-over display.
  *Recommended:* start `GameOverScene` from the demo with `{ demo: true }`,
  render VICTORY/DEFEAT + score without leaderboard qualification or initials,
  and auto-return to the menu after the dwell. Alternative: an outcome overlay
  held in `PlayScene`. Directed to the producer during plan review.
- **OPEN QUESTION (signal transport):** prefer the `CustomEvent` alone, the
  `window.__aiHellRunState` flag alone, or both. *Recommended:* both, with the
  flag as the race fallback (matches the parent risk mitigation). Directed to
  the producer during plan review.

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-07: Initial planning session (downtime dispatch). Pre-check `plan`
  (Small/Medium); approval gate returned `request_approval: false`. Created six
  child work items with dependency edges (contracts → signal → {dwell, capture}
  → verification → docs). Ran the six automated review stages and the AC
  coverage review (100%, `proceed`). Recorded the plan block and two
  producer-facing OPEN QUESTIONs; stage advanced to `plan_complete`.

# Scripted Gameplay Videos (Multi-Scene Capture)

In a scripted video capture we create a level, play it for x seconds, then capture y seconds, pause the video capture. Create a new level, play it for x seconds, capture y seconds. There should be a fade to black and a fade from black lasting 0.25 seconds between each scene. There are an arbitrary number of scenes.

## Problem statement

The current capture system produces a single continuous video — either one full demo run with tail, or a fixed-length scripted clip. This feature adds **multi-scene** capture: sequence several gameplay segments (levels or gyms), play each for a configured duration, capture each for a configured duration, and stitch them into one video with fade transitions (0.25 s black fade in/out) between scenes.

**User story:** As the maintainer, I can define a sequence of scenes and capture each one with play/capture durations and fade transitions, producing a single compiled video showing multiple gameplay segments for demo / showcase / marketing purposes.

## Users

- **Primary — the maintainer / release owner.** Wants to create showcase videos that demonstrate several distinct gameplay elements (different gyms, boss phases, power-up interactions) in one compiled video, rather than multiple separate recordings.

## Existing state

- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — single-scene capture orchestrator
- `scripts/capture-bot.mjs` — scripted bot plan + probe helpers
- `scripts/capture-run-lifecycle.mjs` — run-end signal, tail/cap logic
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.test.ts` — hermetic tests
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — documentation
- `src/scenes/gym/` — individual gym scenes (each exercises one mechanic), discovered dynamically via `import.meta.glob`
- `src/scenes/GymIndex.ts` — dev gym index (reached from the menu's "Gym Scene Index (dev)" control)
- `src/core/devScenario.ts` — URL-selected dev scenarios (`boss-four-hits`, `boss`, `defeat`) with a page-side release handle
- No fade/transition or multi-scene stitching exists in capture tooling.

## Desired change

1. A capture mode that defines a **scene list** (via a config file — see Q1) — each entry specifying the target, play duration (x), and capture duration (y).
2. Between each scene, a **fade-to-black (0.25 s)** then **fade-from-black (0.25 s)** transition is rendered **page-side** and captured by the running recorder.
3. The final output is a **single stitched WebM** containing all scenes with transitions, written to the configured output path.

## Design decisions (producer answers)

- **Q1 — Scene-list specification:** **A (config file).** A JSON config file lists the scenes with their targets and play/capture durations.
- **Q3 — Fade rendering:** **A (page-side canvas overlay).** The fade is drawn over the canvas by the capture (Playwright injection), so the continuously-running `MediaRecorder` captures it and no game-side change is needed. Because one recorder runs across all scenes, scene switching must happen **in-page** (a page reload would end the recorder).
- **Q2 — Scene target:** OPEN — expanded analysis posted in the comment `AH-C0MV0MM81J009GUM6` (options A gym scene keys / B dev scenarios / C generated game levels / D generic scene key; recommended A). Pending producer choice.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — new flags/mode for scene lists
- `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs` (new) — scene-list config parsing, batch orchestration, page-side fade overlay, and single-output stitching
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.test.ts` — new tests for scene parsing, fade timing, and stitch logic
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — documentation
- `src/` — a small dev-gated page-side scene-start hook, if Q2 resolves to A/B/C/D (exact location depends on the Q2 answer)

## Open Questions (need producer review)

**Q2: What does each scene target, and how is it started?** — full analysis in comment `AH-C0MV0MM81J009GUM6`:

- **A.** Gym scene keys (e.g. `GymPlayer`, `GymScout`, `GymWeapons`, `GymBoss`) — widest showcase variety, least per-scene work; dev-only scenes. *(Recommended)*
- **B.** Dev scenarios (e.g. `boss-four-hits`, `defeat`) — real gameplay but verification-oriented; each new variant is a `src/` change.
- **C.** Generated game levels (shipped `PlayScene`, fresh level per scene) — literal match to the brief; multi-wave, needs a dev hook.
- **D.** Arbitrary registered scene key — maximally flexible; best as the internal mechanism, not a separate feature.

## Appendix: Interview Q&A

- **Q1 (Map, to producer): Scene list specification?** — **ANSWERED:** **A** — JSON config file. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 (Map, to producer): Scene target specification?** — **EXPANDED, OPEN.** Options and impacts posted in comment `AH-C0MV0MM81J009GUM6` after producer asked for more detail. Recommended: A (gym scene keys).
- **Q3 (Map, to producer): Fade rendering method?** — **ANSWERED:** **A** — page-side canvas overlay via Playwright. Source: interactive reply.

# Epic: Realistic demo/attract bot framework + playtester telemetry

## Problem

The shipped attract/demo bot (AH-0MUX2NENC008AHOQ and its follow-ups) is a
per-frame priority ladder with a reaction-time governor bolted on. It has no
commitment, no forward model, no aim/fire reasoning and no way to learn from
human play, so it reads as random and cannot be tuned into competence. We need
a **maintainable bot framework** that plays competently and human-like, adapts
to new content (enemies, power-ups, weapons) without a rewrite, can be re-run
headless for reproducible evaluation, and is backed by **telemetry** gathered
both from our own recordings and from production playtesters.

## Goals / user stories

- **As the maintainer**, I can re-run the bot headless on a fixed seed and get
  reproducible results, so I can improve it safely.
- **As the maintainer**, I can add a new enemy / power-up / weapon and have the
  bot handle it through configuration, without touching the core.
- **As the maintainer**, I can record human play and analyse it (reaction
  times, target choices, engagement distances, dodge behaviour) to tune and
  evaluate the bot.
- **As the maintainer**, I can enable opt-in telemetry in production and gather
  playtester data (state + input + events) to improve the bot and the game.
- **As a player**, I see an attract/demo mode that looks like a competent
  player.

## Design overview

- **Determinism.** A per-run **seed** drives all gameplay RNG (wave/spawn/
  timing) so a run is reproducible and the bot can be evaluated same-seed.
- **Telemetry.** A **versioned, consent-gated, pluggable** pipeline. Records
  are per-tick state + input + discrete events, tagged with the run seed and a
  schema version. Sinks: a local JSONL dev sink and a production remote sink.
  No PII; **disabled by default in production**, opt-in only.
- **Bot framework.** A world model (from `BotSnapshot`), a **registry of
  goals/behaviours**, a **utility selector with commitment/hysteresis**, a
  behaviour-tree executor, and predictive **dodge/aim** behaviours.
  Content-specific parameters live in a **config/registry** so new content is
  data, not code.
- **Evaluation.** Same-seed bot-vs-human runs, metrics, A/B comparisons and
  side-by-side clips.
- **Style matching (later).** Fit parameters or train a policy from recorded
  telemetry once the competent bot exists.

## Epic acceptance criteria

- **AC1:** Runs are reproducible from a seed; the seed is recorded in
  telemetry; a headless runner executes the bot for N ticks on a seed and
  produces a deterministic report.
- **AC2:** Telemetry is a pluggable framework with a documented, versioned
  schema, disabled by default in production and opt-in consent-gated; it
  records per-tick state + input + events with the seed and is a no-op when
  disabled.
- **AC3:** The bot is a structured framework (world model + goal/behaviour
  registry + committed selection + predictive dodge/aim), not a per-frame
  priority ladder; new enemies/power-ups/weapons are handled via config with
  tests.
- **AC4:** The competent bot completes representative runs with human-like
  behaviour (goal commitment, no suicide, human cadence) and passes an
  evaluation report (survival, minerals/min, targets engaged, dodges).
- **AC5:** Human play can be recorded and analysed offline, and a replay/ghost
  viewer compares bot vs human on the same seed.
- **AC6:** Production telemetry can be enabled by a playtester via an explicit
  opt-in, with privacy documentation and no PII.
- **AC7:** All documentation is updated (framework, extension guide, telemetry
  schema/privacy); full suite, typecheck and build pass.

## Out of scope (this epic)

- A fully style-matched clone of a specific player (style matching is an
  early-phase deliverable; full fidelity is a later follow-up).
- Server-side ML training infrastructure or online multiplayer.
- CI wiring of the capture/eval jobs (follow-up once the harness exists).

## Children (dependency order)

1. Deterministic run seeding + seed plumbing.
2. Telemetry framework (versioned schema, pluggable sinks, consent flag).
3. Game telemetry instrumentation (per-tick state + events).
4. Dev recording, analysis and replay/ghost tooling.
5. Bot framework core (world model, goal/behaviour registry, committed policy,
   content config).
6. Structured competent bot (utility goals + behaviour tree + predictive
   dodge/aim).
7. Content-adaptive configuration for enemies, power-ups and weapons.
8. Same-seed evaluation harness (metrics, A/B, side-by-side clips).
9. Style matching from telemetry (parameter fitting / imitation).
10. Production telemetry (opt-in consent, privacy, remote sink, docs).

## Related work

Builds on AH-0MUX2NENC008AHOQ (Smart capture bot) and its follow-ups
AH-0MUXXQ1MN002RXGB (human-like input) and AH-0MUXYOV4C008MV0L (movement
goals). Supersedes the per-frame priority-ladder design.

## Summary
Build the **telemetry framework**: a versioned, consent-gated, pluggable pipeline that is a strict no-op unless enabled. It must work identically in dev and production and be safe/privacy-preserving.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1: A `TelemetryRecorder` interface with versioned record schemas (run header with seed/schema version/build; per-tick state+input; discrete events).
- AC2: Pluggable sinks behind one interface: a local JSONL dev sink and a remote/production sink stub; a no-op sink used when disabled.
- AC3: **Disabled by default**; explicitly enabled via config/env. A consent flag gates production recording.
- AC4: Bounded overhead/backpressure (ring buffer + batched flush) so recording never stalls gameplay; a documented sampling option.
- AC5: No PII in the schema; secrets/tokens excluded; documented data policy.
- AC6: Unit tests: no-op sink records nothing; JSONL sink round-trips; batching/flush; schema version present.
- AC7: Docs: schema reference + how to enable/disable.
data.title: Telemetry framework: versioned schema, pluggable sinks, consent flag

data.description:
## Summary
Instrument the game so a run emits telemetry: per-tick state plus discrete events, tagged with the run seed and schema version. Must cover both human play and the bot, and must not affect gameplay.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1: Each tick records a compact state vector (player pos/vel/heading, hold/levels, enemies, enemy bullets, drops, minerals, boss) reusing the existing `BotSnapshot` builder where possible.
- AC2: The human/bot input for the tick is recorded alongside the state (the input actually applied).
- AC3: Discrete events are recorded: run start (seed), deaths/hits, pickups, hold-full choice + selection, wave/level transitions, boss phase, run end (win/lose).
- AC4: Recording works when the bot drives and when a human drives, in `PlayScene`; shared-core scenes can opt in.
- AC5: Overhead is bounded and gameplay is unchanged (regression tests); telemetry off = zero records.
- AC6: Unit tests for the state/event serialisation and seed/version tagging.
data.title: Game telemetry instrumentation: per-tick state and events

## Summary
Dev tooling to record a human session, analyse it offline and replay/ghost it against the bot — the data loop for tuning and evaluating the bot.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1: A dev command/mode records a human session to JSONL (state + input + events + seed) using the telemetry framework.
- AC2: An offline analysis script produces a report: key-hold duration histogram, input-change cadence, reaction latency proxy, target-choice stats (mineral/power-up/enemy), engagement distances, dodge outcomes, survival/minerals-per-minute.
- AC3: A replay/ghost viewer steps a recording deterministically and overlays human vs bot input/position (same seed).
- AC4: The recorded dataset is versioned and documented so scripts can evolve with the schema.
- AC5: Tests for the analyser (pure stats) and the replay stepping.
- AC6: Docs: how to record, analyse and replay.
data.title: Dev recording, analysis and replay/ghost tooling

data.description:
## Summary
Replace the per-frame priority ladder with a **bot framework**: a world model, a registry of goals/behaviours, a committed policy and a content configuration seam. This is the maintainable core that later content and styles plug into.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1: A `BotBrain`/policy interface that maps a `BotSnapshot` (+ world model + memory) to an input, with an explicit **commitment** mechanism (a selected goal is held until achieved, invalidated, or outranked by a margin for a minimum time).
- AC2: A **goal/behaviour registry**: goals and behaviours register by id; adding one does not require editing the core switch/if-chain.
- AC3: A world-model/predictor layer (positions/velocities, incoming-fire prediction) separated from decision policy, so prediction is testable in isolation.
- AC4: The existing pure `decideBotInput` is preserved behind an adapter (so current tests/gyms keep working) or cleanly superseded with documented parity tests.
- AC5: The framework is deterministic and pure over an injected `dt`/clock; no wall-clock dependence.
- AC6: Unit tests: registry, commitment/hysteresis, deterministic replay of a decision sequence.
- AC7: Docs: framework overview + how goals/behaviours are structured.
data.title: Bot framework core: world model, goal/behaviour registry, committed policy

data.description:
## Summary
Implement the **competent** structured bot on top of the framework: utility-based goal selection with commitment, behaviour-tree execution (seek → line up → engage/collect → dodge), explicit aim/fire reasoning and predictive dodging. Competent first; style matching comes later.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1: Goal set covering the operator's order (minerals > power-ups > enemies > asteroids) plus survival, each as a registered goal with a utility/priority and hysteresis.
- AC2: Behaviours: collect (approach + scoop), engage enemy, engage asteroid, evade (predictive path-around, not just direction rejection), reposition/idle.
- AC3: **Aim/fire reasoning**: the bot positions to line up a target while dodging, rather than only aiming by accident of movement.
- AC4: Survival is a hard constraint: never-suicide property tests over sampled snapshots; no wall/enemy/bullet/asteroid collision when a safe alternative exists.
- AC5: Human-like cadence: committed input changes no faster than the human-like toggles; tunables single-sourced.
- AC6: The competent bot completes a representative run (survives/destroys enough) and beats the old ladder on an evaluation metric.
- AC7: Deterministic unit tests per goal/behaviour; integration test on a seeded run.
- AC8: Docs updated (the new decision model).
data.title: Structured competent bot: utility goals, behaviour tree, predictive dodge/aim

data.description:
## Summary
Make the bot **content-adaptive**: new enemies, power-ups and weapons should be handled via configuration, not core changes, so the bot keeps working as the game grows.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1: A content config/registry describes, per enemy archetype, threat value, preferred engagement range, aim/lead behaviour and whether it is an asteroid-like hazard.
- AC2: Power-up and weapon definitions declare bot-relevant value/priority (e.g. collection desirability) consumed by the goal scorer.
- AC3: Adding a new enemy/power-up/weapon requires only a config entry (plus its game data) — demonstrated by a test that registers a synthetic content type and the bot handles it.
- AC4: Unknown content degrades gracefully (documented default).
- AC5: Unit tests for the config lookup and the synthetic-content path.
- AC6: Docs: "how to teach the bot about new content".
data.title: Content-adaptive configuration for enemies, power-ups and weapons

## Summary
A reproducible evaluation harness: run the bot (and replay a human recording) on the same seed, produce metrics, A/B two bot versions, and render side-by-side clips. This is how we "re-run the bot production code" after changes.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1: A headless runner executes the bot for N ticks/seeds and emits a deterministic report (from telemetry).
- AC2: Same-seed comparison: bot vs human recording, and bot-vs-bot across versions, with metrics (survival time, minerals/min, power-ups, enemies/asteroids destroyed, avoidable hits, input cadence).
- AC3: A/B runner compares two bot configs/versions and reports the difference with confidence (multiple seeds).
- AC4: Optional side-by-side video via the existing capture tooling.
- AC5: Results are reproducible (same seed + config → same report) and stored as artifacts.
- AC6: Tests for the runner/report (pure aggregation) and determinism.
- AC7: Docs: how to run evaluations and interpret the report.
data.title: Same-seed evaluation harness: metrics, A/B, side-by-side

data.description:
## Summary
Later phase: make the bot **match a player's style** using recorded telemetry (parameter fitting and/or behaviour cloning), on top of the competent framework.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1: A pipeline that extracts style features from human recordings (reaction latency, hold distribution, target preferences, engagement distances, risk appetite).
- AC2: A parameter-fitting path that maps those features onto the structured bot's tunables (preferred first; keeps safety guarantees).
- AC3: (Optional/stretch) A behaviour-cloning policy trained from `(state → input)` pairs, evaluated against the structured bot on the same seeds.
- AC4: Evaluation shows the styled bot is measurably closer to the human recording than the default competent bot, without regressing competence/survival.
- AC5: Docs: how to train/fit and evaluate a style.
- AC6: Tests for the feature extraction (pure).

## Notes
Depends on the recording/analysis tooling and the evaluation harness. Lower priority than competence.
data.title: Style matching from telemetry (parameter fitting / imitation)

## Summary
Turn on telemetry in **production** for playtesters: an explicit opt-in consent flow, privacy-safe records, batched upload to a remote sink, and documentation.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1: An in-game consent/opt-in prompt (and a settings toggle) gating production telemetry; default **off**; easy opt-out.
- AC2: A remote sink that batches and uploads records (endpoint configurable), with retry/backoff and no gameplay impact when offline.
- AC3: Records are PII-free and documented; a data-retention/privacy note is included in the docs and (if applicable) the consent screen.
- AC4: A remote-off/no-op path so local dev and offline play are unaffected (tests).
- AC5: A simple way to inspect downloaded telemetry (reuse the analysis tooling from child 4).
- AC6: Tests for consent gating, the uploader's batching/backoff, and the disabled path.
- AC7: Docs: telemetry privacy + how playtester data is stored and used.

# Intake Brief — Enhance Central AI boss encounter

**Work item:** Enhance Central AI boss encounter: 200 HP, more minions, figure-8 movement, top-screen health bar, hit feedback (AH-0MUY3X4NS007JR8X)

## Problem statement

The Central AI boss encounter is currently a static, 400-hit grind: the boss does not move, the health bar is drawn relative to the boss container (so it is visibly displaced rather than at the top of the screen), and individual hits give no feedback beyond a bullet disappearing. Players cannot read their progress and the fight lacks the mobility and impact expected of a climactic boss. This work item reduces the boss's total health to **200**, reinforces the fight with **more minions**, gives the boss **figure-of-8 movement**, fixes the **health bar to the top of the screen**, and makes **every hit obvious through SFX and VFX**.

## Users

- **Player (primary):** fights the boss after clearing Level 5 and wants a readable, impactful, mobile encounter.
  - *As a player, I want to see the boss's health decrease with every hit so I know my shots are registering.*
  - *As a player, I want the fight to feel dynamic and dangerous, with the boss moving and more enemies on screen.*
  - *As a player, I want clear audio/visual feedback on each hit so the encounter feels responsive.*
- **Developer/maintainer (secondary):** wants the change implemented once in the shared core so the game and boss gyms stay in parity.
  - *As a developer, I want the boss behaviour to live in the shared core so `PlayScene` and `GymBoss` cannot diverge.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Boss total health is 200.** The boss spawns with 200 total hits across the existing **4 phases (50 hits per phase)**. The 4-phase structure, phase transitions, and score/minion rewards gated on *depleting* hits are preserved. Verified by unit tests: hit 49 stays in phase 1, hit 50 advances to phase 2, and hit 200 destroys the boss.
- **More minions are spawned with the boss.** Phase 1 spawns **12 scouts** (6 per side), phase 2 spawns **12 divers** (6 per side), phase 3 remains **0** (the pulse is the threat), and phase 4 spawns **15 swarm**. Verified by `BossMinions` unit tests asserting the per-phase counts via `minionCountForPhase`.
- **The boss moves in a figure-of-8 pattern.** The boss traces a lemniscate around its spawn anchor (≈120 px horizontal, ≈60 px vertical amplitude, ≈8 s per full cycle), staying within the playfield. Movement is implemented once in the shared boss/combat core and is identical in `PlayScene` and every boss gym. Hit detection continues to use the boss's live position, and the health bar does not move with it. Verified by tests asserting the traced position and bounded amplitude.
- **The health bar is fixed at the top of the screen and decreases per hit.** The bar is camera-fixed, horizontally centred at the top of the playfield, always visible during the encounter, and **not** offset or moved by the boss's figure-8 motion. Its fill shrinks proportionally on every hit (200 → 0) with the four phase-segment dividers retained. Verified by tests asserting the bar's screen position is independent of the boss position and that `getHpFraction()` decreases after hits.
- **Hits on the boss are obvious with both SFX and VFX.** Every hit on the boss plays a dedicated boss-hit SFX cue and spawns an obvious impact VFX (flash/burst) at the hit point; phase transitions retain their existing distinct cue and visual. Game and gym use the same shared feedback path. Verified by the cue-manifest contract test (new cue registered) and VFX tests (an impact effect is registered per hit).
- **Test coverage.** New/updated tests cover the health model, minion counts, figure-8 motion, health-bar placement, and hit feedback across `Boss.test.ts`, `BossMinions.test.ts`, `GymBoss.test.ts`, `PlayScene.test.ts`, and the audio cue contract.
- **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, the Game Design Document (§4.3), `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (§5.1 parity), and the audio cue mapping/manifest.
- **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (mandatory):** gameplay behaviour must live in the shared core (`src/scenes/core/`, `src/entities/`) and be consumed by both `PlayScene` and `GymBoss`; no divergent copies. The `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` duplicate-body guard and gym-parity docs assertion must still pass.
- **Preserve the 4-phase model:** do not change the phase attack patterns, telegraphs, or reward gating; only retune totals/counts and add movement/feedback.
- **Health bar model:** keep the existing proportional `getHpFraction()` fill and the four phase-segment dividers.
- **Audio pipeline:** a new SFX cue must be registered in `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` and `src/audio/cueManifest.ts` (the contract test enforces completeness).
- **No new dependencies.**
- Stay within the existing visual/neon style and UK-English documentation conventions.

## Existing state

- `src/entities/Boss.ts`: 4 phases × `BOSS_HIT_POINTS_PER_PHASE = 100` = **400 total hits**; `applyFormationPosition()` is a static `setPosition(baseX, baseY)`; `healthBarGraphics` is added as a **child of the boss container** but drawn with screen coordinates (so it renders offset by the boss position); `takeDamage()` only plays the phase-transition cue on a depleting hit; no per-hit feedback.
- `src/waves/BossMinions.ts`: phase 1 = 8 scouts (4+4), phase 2 = 8 divers (4+4), phase 3 = 0, phase 4 = 10 swarm.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` `_damageBoss()`: applies damage and awards score/summons minions on phase depletion; no hit SFX/VFX.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts` `damageBoss()`: gym equivalent, mirrors the game's gating.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` `_advanceBoss()`: shared per-frame boss advance consumed by both the game and the gym (the correct place for shared movement/feedback).
- `src/vfx/bulletImpact.ts`: reusable `spawnBulletImpact()` flash already used for non-lethal hits on multi-hit enemies (Harvester) but **not** wired to the boss.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` + `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` + `src/audio/cueManifest.ts`: no boss-hit cue exists.
- Docs: `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.3 documents the 400-hit model and static boss.

## Desired change

1. Retune boss health to a **200-hit total** (4 phases × 50) and update the constants/comments/tests.
2. Increase minion counts to **P1 = 12, P2 = 12, P3 = 0, P4 = 15**.
3. Add **figure-8 (lemniscate) movement** around the spawn anchor in the shared boss core, with parameters ≈120 px / ≈60 px / ≈8 s, bounded to the playfield.
4. **Re-parent the health bar** out of the boss container so it is camera-fixed at the top-centre of the screen, always visible, and unaffected by boss movement; keep the proportional fill and phase dividers.
5. Add a **dedicated boss-hit SFX cue** and an **obvious hit VFX** (impact flash/burst at the hit point) applied on every hit through a shared path used by both the game and the gym; keep the existing phase-transition feedback.
6. Update tests and documentation (GDD, enemy design/parity doc, audio mapping).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/entities/Boss.ts` — health constants (50/phase, 200 total), figure-8 movement, health-bar re-parenting/positioning, per-hit feedback hook.
- `src/waves/BossMinions.ts` — increased per-phase minion counts.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — shared boss movement/feedback seam for parity.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_damageBoss()` hit-feedback wiring; health-bar layering.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts` — `damageBoss()` hit-feedback wiring (parity).
- `src/audio/effects.ts`, `audio/toneforge/manifest.json`, `src/audio/cueManifest.ts` — new boss-hit cue and mapping.
- `src/vfx/bulletImpact.ts` — reusable/extended impact flash for boss hits.
- `src/entities/Boss.test.ts`, `src/waves/BossMinions.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/audio/cueManifest.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — tests.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — documentation updates.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUUJEB1D000GPX0** – PlayScene/GymBoss reward gating on phase depletion (completed) — established the `phaseAdvanced`-gated score/minion behaviour this work preserves.
- **AH-0MUUJCL8J00632T7** – Boss.ts per-phase HP model, return contract, health-bar fill (completed) — the `getHpFraction()` proportional fill this work keeps.
- **AH-0MUTV3J7T006MZ4K** – Increase Central AI boss hits-per-phase 10x (completed) — prior health tuning precedent.
- **AH-0MT99QBDW001O7PE** – Create Boss (Central AI) gym scene (completed) — gym that must stay in parity.
- **AH-0MU730M3T008C7CQ** – Integrate boss encounter into PlayScene (completed) — boss spawn wiring and minion sums.
- **AH-0MUD9R3ZC0006M4I** – Extract collision core and host bullet-vs-bullet impact feedback (completed) — shared impact-feedback precedent.

### Related work (automated report)

- **AH-0MUUJEB1D000GPX0** – PlayScene/GymBoss reward gating on phase depletion (completed)
- **AH-0MU3X86GT001YM5D** – Identify enemy refactor opportunities (completed)
- **AH-0MUUJFOTM009ORQM** – GDD and code comment documentation updates (AC7) (completed)

Repository file matches: `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `README.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (confirmed):** "200 health" means 200 total hits across 4 phases (50 each), not 200 per phase.
- **Assumption (confirmed):** minion increase ≈50% in phases 1, 2 and 4; phase 3 stays minion-free.
- **Assumption (confirmed):** figure-8 defaults 120 px / 60 px / ~8 s; boss-only motion; top-centre screen-fixed health bar; new per-hit SFX + impact-flash VFX.
- **Risk:** figure-8 motion could push the boss off-screen or desync aimed shots/minions — mitigate with bounded amplitude and using the boss's live position for aiming/collision.
- **Risk:** health-bar re-parenting may break tests that assume the bar is a container child — update those tests and add explicit screen-position assertions.
- **Risk:** the new SFX may need a ToneForge recipe/baked asset; if a new recipe is required the audio build pipeline must render it (or reuse an existing recipe) and the manifest must stay complete so the contract test passes.
- **Risk:** gameplay change requires parity across `PlayScene` and all boss gyms — implement in shared core only; verify with the equivalence/parity tests.
- **Scope-creep:** further boss rebalancing (attack patterns, telegraph timings, additional phases) is out of scope; record as separate work items if raised.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1: What does "reduce the health to 200" mean?** Options: (a) 200 total hits across 4 phases (50 each); (b) 200 per phase (800 total); (c) other. **Recommended:** (a) — preserves the 4-phase model.
  - **Answer (operator):** "(a)". Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-07.
- **Q2: How much should the minion count increase, and in which phases?** Options: (a) ~50% more in phases 1, 2 and 4 (P1 12, P2 12, P3 0, P4 15); (b) roughly double all; (c) add minions to phase 3; (d) other. **Recommended:** (a).
  - **Answer (operator):** "(a)". Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-07.
- **Q3: Are the implementation defaults acceptable?** (figure-8: 120 px / 60 px / ~8 s, boss-only; hit feedback: new hit SFX + impact flash on every hit, keeping phase-transition feedback; health bar: screen-fixed top-centre). **Recommended:** accept.
  - **Answer (operator):** "yes". Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-07.
data.title: Enhance Central AI boss encounter: 200 HP, more minions, figure-8 movement, top-screen health bar, hit feedback

# Add 10% weighting to owned upgrades in hold-full choice

## Problem statement

When the hold fills and the player is offered a choice of upgrades, owned upgrades (weapon-level / power-up-level options) should appear 10% more likely than they currently do. Currently all candidates are selected uniformly at random; owned upgrades should receive a 1.1× weight multiplier.

## Users

- **Player (progression):** "As a player, when offered a hold-full choice I want a reasonable chance of upgrading an upgradeable weapon or power-up I already own, so my build keeps improving rather than forcing me to chase new items."
- **Designer:** "As a designer, I want owned upgrades to appear 10% more often so progression feels steady across runs."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — 10% weighting.** Owned level-up offers (both `weapon-level` and `power-up-level`) have a 1.1× weight multiplier applied during candidate selection. Unowned (base-pool) items retain 1.0× weight.
- **AC2 — Single source of truth.** The weighting logic lives in the strategy layer (`createRandomChoiceStrategy`), not in `buildChoiceCandidates`; no duplicate weighting code in scenes or gyms.
- **AC3 — Gym↔game parity.** The behaviour is identical in `PlayScene` and every gym that opens the hold-full choice, because they share `MineralChoiceScene` and `powerups/choice`.
- **AC4 — Configurable weight.** The 1.1× multiplier is a named constant (e.g. `OWNED_UPGRADE_BONUS_WEIGHT = 1.1`) so it can be tuned later without hunting for magic numbers.
- **AC5 — Testing/validation.** Unit tests verify: (a) owned-level candidates receive 1.1× weight; (b) weighted random selection produces the expected distribution (10,000 trials, ±3% tolerance, owned items appear ~10% more often than unowned items relative to pool size); (c) gym↔game parity tests pass.
- **AC6 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **AC7 — Full suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes. (CI/CD pipeline tests are out of scope.)

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md):** shared behaviour must live once and be consumed by both the game and every gym.
- **Backward compatible:** no breaking changes to the `ChoiceStrategy` interface or existing `ChoiceOption` consumers.
- **No gameplay logic changes beyond weighting:** the candidate list itself is unchanged — only the selection probabilities shift.
- **Run-scoped:** no leaderboard impact.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — add weighting logic in `createRandomChoiceStrategy`.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.ts` — no changes expected (they already pass context).
- `src/powerups/__tests__/choice.test.ts` — new tests for weighted selection (10k trials, ±3%).
- `src/scenes/__tests__/MineralChoiceScene.test.ts` — parity tests.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR** — Show upgrade change summary and New badge in the hold-full choice list (completed).
- **AH-0MUPMPCB2009J54J** — Weapon leveling (completed).
- **AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q** — Asteroids drop collectable minerals that fill the ship'\''s hold (completed).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Statistical testing (low):** proving 10% bias requires many trials; tests use 10,000 draws with ±3% tolerance band.
- **Scope creep (low):** adding per-weight tunability (player-facing weight editor) could expand scope. Mitigation: this item implements a single constant only; per-weight tuning is a separate chore if needed.
- **Assumption:** "10% more likely" means a 1.1× multiplicative weight, not an additive 10 percentage points.
- **Assumption:** "owned upgrade" means `weapon-level` and `power-up-level` kind options in the candidate list.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Scope of owned upgrades?** (A: both weapon-level and power-up-level; B: only weapon-level; C: both with different weights.) — Answer (Producer): A — both weapon-level and power-up-level.
- **Q2 — Where does weighting logic live?** (A: in `buildChoiceCandidates` with tagged weights; B: in `createRandomChoiceStrategy` strategy layer.) — Answer (Producer): B — in the strategy layer.
- **Q3 — Test tolerance for statistical validation?** (A: 10,000 trials, ±3%; B: 50,000 trials, ±1%; C: 5,000 trials, ±5%.) — Answer (Producer): A — 10,000 trials, ±3%.
data.title: Add 10% weighting to owned upgrades in hold-full choice

# Flaky PlayScene AC4 victory-celebration SHUTDOWN test under heavy load

**Headline:** Two `PlayScene` victory/transition tests wait on a wall-clock
`setTimeout(VICTORY_TRANSITION_HOLD_MS + 500)` and race Phaser's delayed
`GameOverScene` transition under heavy machine load; make them advance the
Phaser clock deterministically so the full suite is trustworthy again.

## Problem statement

`src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` contains two tests that assert the run has
transitioned to `GameOverScene` (or that the victory celebration has been
torn down) by sleeping a real `VICTORY_TRANSITION_HOLD_MS + 500` ms and then
asserting on live scene state. The production transition is a Phaser
`this.time.delayedCall(VICTORY_TRANSITION_HOLD_MS, …)`; under CPU/timer
contention the wall-clock sleep can expire before the scene clock has
advanced far enough, so the assertion observes the pre-transition state.

- Reported failure (2026-10-07, full suite under heavy multi-agent load):
  `Tests 1 failed | 3509 passed` at the AC4 SHUTDOWN assertion
  (`expect(effect.active).toBe(false)`), then **passed on immediate re-run**
  (`152 files / 3510 tests passed`).
- The flake is test-harness nondeterminism, not a production defect: the
  live requestAnimationFrame loop advances the scene by an amount that depends
  on machine load, so a fixed real-time wait is not a reliable barrier.

## Users

- **Test maintainers / release engineers:** need a green full suite so a
  random failure does not mask a real regression or block `dev` → `main`.
- **Developers:** need to add/extend victory and teardown tests without
  inheriting a load-sensitive sleep.

**Example user stories**

- As a developer, I want the victory-transition tests to be deterministic
  under load, so a full-suite run is a trustworthy signal.
- As a release engineer, I want flaky PlayScene tests eliminated, so the
  release pipeline is not blocked by a phantom failure.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Deterministic clock:** Neither affected test depends on a
  wall-clock `setTimeout` that can be missed under load. Each advances the
  Phaser clock deterministically (stop the live loop and pump the scene clock,
  e.g. `game.loop.stop()` + `game.step(simTime, STEP_MS)` / a `stepUntil`
  predicate) **or** waits on the scene/transition state rather than elapsed
  real time.
- **AC2 — Repeatable under load:** The affected tests pass deterministically
  when the full suite is run **3 consecutive times** on a loaded machine (or
  with elevated `--maxConcurrency`), with zero failures attributable to these
  tests.
- **AC3 — No regressions:** No other PlayScene (or other suite) tests regress,
  and production behaviour — the `VICTORY_TRANSITION_HOLD_MS` victory hold and
  the `SHUTDOWN` teardown of the celebration — is unchanged.
- **AC4 — Test/validation coverage:** The fix includes a meaningful
  testing/validation criterion that exercises the deterministic path (i.e. the
  test itself proves the transition/teardown without relying on elapsed wall
  time), and the pattern is documented where a future author can reuse it.
- **AC5 — Documentation:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
  changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site
  entries. (CHANGELOG.md is out of scope — owned by the ship release pipeline.)
- **AC6 — Full suite:** Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Test-harness only:** do not change production `PlayScene` victory/teardown
  behaviour; only the test harness (and, at most, a clarifying production
  comment) may change. Preserve `deterministicBoot: true`.
- **No meaningful slowdown:** the deterministic stepping must not materially
  increase suite runtime.
- **Reuse existing patterns:** mirror the established `game.step` +
  `stepUntil` approach already used in `PlaySceneSeeding.test.ts` and
  `PlaySceneTelemetry.test.ts` rather than inventing a new mechanism.
- **Gym↔game parity:** not applicable — this is a test harness change with no
  gameplay behaviour change (`docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §5.1).
- **UK English** in all comments and documentation.
- **Isolation:** keep the change scoped to the failure; do not fold in
  unrelated test refactors.

## Existing state

- `VICTORY_TRANSITION_HOLD_MS = ENDOFRUN_VICTORY_FIREWORKS_DURATION_MS`
  (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` ≈ line 240).
- `_finishRunWithPurpose(won)` schedules the transition via
  `this.time.delayedCall(VICTORY_TRANSITION_HOLD_MS, () => this._finishRun(won))`
  (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` ≈ line 1690). Its doc comment already notes that a
  zero hold transitions immediately to keep timing tests deterministic.
- **Two** tests use the wall-clock pattern `await new Promise((r) =>
  setTimeout(r, VICTORY_TRANSITION_HOLD_MS + 500))`:
  1. `PlayScene — boss encounter` → **"AC4 — defeating all 4 phases wins the
     run at the game-over screen"** (`src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` ≈ line 1613).
  2. `PlayScene — end-of-run victory trigger` → **"AC4 — the victory
     celebration is destroyed on SHUTDOWN (no leaks)"**
     (`src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` ≈ line 3923) — the reported failure.
- Established deterministic stepping already exists:
  `booted.game.loop.stop()` + `game.step(simTime, STEP_MS)` and a `stepUntil`
  predicate (`src/scenes/PlaySceneSeeding.test.ts` ≈ lines 55–70;
  `src/scenes/PlaySceneTelemetry.test.ts` ≈ lines 80–90).
- Precedent: `reachBoss()` was previously made load-robust by polling the
  `WaveManager` flags instead of `getBoss()` (AH-0MUNVVWWC0015JTM).

## Desired change

Replace both wall-clock waits with deterministic Phaser-clock advancement
(stop the live loop and step a fixed simulated time past
`VICTORY_TRANSITION_HOLD_MS`, or poll a scene/transition predicate with a hard
failure message), so the tests assert the same behaviour without depending on
real elapsed time. Keep assertions and coverage identical; document the
deterministic pattern at the point of use.

## Validation approach

- Target only the affected tests while iterating:
  `npx vitest run src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts -t "AC4"`
- Prove repeatability under load (AC2): run the full suite three times with
  elevated concurrency:
  `for i in 1 2 3; do npm test -- --maxConcurrency 50 || exit 1; done`
- Confirm production behaviour is untouched: `git diff src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`
  shows comment-only changes (or nothing).
- Final gate: run the full suite via `/skill:test` before `in_review`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — replace the two
  `setTimeout(VICTORY_TRANSITION_HOLD_MS + 500)` waits (≈ lines 1613 and
  3923) with deterministic clock advancement / state polling; possibly add a
  small shared `stepPastVictoryHold` helper.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — reference only; `_finishRunWithPurpose` (≈ line
  1690) documents the hold. Production logic unchanged.
- `src/scenes/PlaySceneSeeding.test.ts` / `src/scenes/PlaySceneTelemetry.test.ts`
  — existing `game.step` + `stepUntil` patterns to mirror (reference only).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption A1 (scope):** Both wall-clock waits share the same root cause,
  so both are fixed in this work item; fixing only the reported AC4 SHUTDOWN
  test would leave an identical load-sensitive flake behind. Recorded for
  producer confirmation.
- **Assumption A2:** The flake is harness nondeterminism, not a production
  race — supported by the pass-on-rerun evidence and the existing zero-hold
  deterministic hook. If stepping the clock exposes a genuine ordering bug,
  raise a separate work item rather than widening this one.
- **Risk R1 — clock semantics:** Phaser's `Clock` advances through
  `game.step`; a naive `scene.tick()` loop may not advance `delayedCall`. The
  fix must verify which driver advances the timer.
- **Risk R2 — stepping budget:** An unbounded step loop could hide a stalled
  transition; use a bounded `stepUntil` predicate that fails loudly.
- **Risk R3 — scope creep:** Additional flaky waits discovered elsewhere
  should become linked work items (`discovered-from:`), not be folded in.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUZMTU3Y001Y8XZ** – Verify gym-game parity and full test suite (blocked)
- **AH-0MUNVVWWC0015JTM** – Flaky tests: PlayScene and GymFormationScene fail intermittently under full-suite parallel load (completed)
- **AH-0MUWTNPY8003GGAA** – capture: add progress/ETA output and dependency preflight (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: ac1, ac3, ac4, acceptance, active (+69 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: ac1, ac3, ac4, active, agent (+64 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, active (+59 more)

**Manual cross-references**

- **AH-0MUNVVWWC0015JTM** — closest precedent: deterministic makeover of
  `PlayScene` boss tests (`reachBoss` flag polling) after full-suite parallel
  flakiness; the same load-sensitivity root cause.
- **AH-0MUXZ4D0M001IWW1** — `discovered-from` parent (full-run capture
  integration verification); this item was discovered during that run.
- **AH-0MUZMTU3Y001Y8XZ** — "Verify gym-game parity and full test suite"
  (blocked): consumes a trustworthy full suite; a green suite here unblocks the
  evidence that item needs.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Clarifying questions:** none required — the seed context (problem,
  reproduction, expected behaviour and a concrete implementation sketch)
  was sufficient to draft this brief without an interview round.
- **Assumption A1 (recorded, not a question):** both wall-clock waits are
  treated as in scope; see Risks and assumptions above.
- **Assumption A2 (recorded, not a question):** harness-only fix; production
  behaviour unchanged.

# Intake Brief — Research classic enemies from the arcade games of old

## Problem statement

AI_Hell's enemy roster (E1–E7) is a coherent but self-contained set of
formations. It does not yet deliberately mine the **classic arcade era** for
signature, instantly-recognisable enemy behaviours. This epic researches that
era and turns the best candidates into implementable work items, so the game
can grow a distinctive "arcade homage" roster without ad-hoc, un-scoped enemy
requests.

## Users

- **As the game designer**, I want a researched, curated catalogue of classic
  arcade enemy behaviours adapted to AI_Hell's neon-vector rules, so that new
  enemy work starts from a clear design brief rather than a one-line wish.
- **As an implementing agent/developer**, I want each selected enemy to have
  its own work item with a user story, testable ACs, predicted key files and a
  plan that follows the existing data-driven enemy convention, so I can
  implement it without re-deriving the design.
- **As the producer**, I want the candidates that were considered but not
  selected recorded, so the roster can be expanded later without redoing the
  research.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A research document `docs/CLASSIC_ENEMY_RESEARCH.md` exists and catalogues at least 5 and at most 8 selected classic arcade enemy archetypes, recording for each its source game, original behaviour, adaptation to AI_Hell's neon-vector code-drawn no-enemy-collision rules, and why it was selected.
- The research document includes a considered but not selected section listing the remaining candidates from the research pool, each with a one-line reason for deferral, so the range can be expanded later.
- One child work item exists per selected archetype, each containing a user story, measurable and testable acceptance criteria including unit tests, predicted key files, and a plan that follows section 8.6 Adding a new enemy in `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, and each child references this epic and the research document.
- Each selected archetype's design notes specify how it fits the data-driven pipeline, whether it is expressible as an `EnemyConfig`/CSV row or needs a new `src/entities/<Name>.ts` plus factory/fire-dispatch seam, and give its enemy difficulty scoring inputs for movement, fire and health factors.
- Each selected archetype's notes name the gym scenes that will exercise it, existing `GymEnemies` or a new gym, to satisfy the gym-to-game parity rule.
- Validation checks the research document recommendations against existing engine constraints so every selected archetype maps to an existing or explicitly-planned formation/shot-pattern registry entry, and every child work item carries explicit unit-test acceptance criteria.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Neon-vector aesthetic, code-drawn graphics only** — no external art assets
  (GDD §7.2).
- **Gym↔game parity** — an enabled gameplay object must run the same code in a
  gym and the game; shared behaviour lives in `src/scenes/core/`. Enforced by
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` and the gym-parity docs
  assertion (AGENTS.md).
- **Data-driven enemies** — tuning is data, not code; archetypes are rows in
  `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` (AH-0MTFP7EIC004F1MN). A genuinely new entity is
  only justified when the existing formation/shot registries cannot express it.
- **"Enemies are the bullets" design** (GDD §2.4) and **no enemy–enemy
  collisions** (GDD §2.6).
- **Behaviours must be adaptable to a top-down free-2D arena** — the original
  arcade games are lane/axis-based; the brief must state how each archetype is
  translated (or note where translation is not faithful).
- **Scope is research + design + child-item creation.** This epic does not
  itself implement the enemies; each selected archetype's implementation is its
  own child work item.

## Existing state

- **Enemy catalog** (GDD §4.1, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §1):
  E1 Scout, E2 Diver, E3 Tank, E4 Phaser, E5 Swarm, E6 Asteroid, E7 Harvester,
  plus the multi-phase Boss.
- **Enemy implementation guide** `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`
  documents the shared core scene library, the CSV pipeline (§8), and the
  "adding a new enemy" checklist (§8.6).
- **Data-driven pipeline**: `src/core/enemyConfig.ts`, `src/core/configTypes.ts`,
  `src/core/configDefaults.ts`, `src/data/enemy-configs.csv`,
  `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts`, `src/entities/enemyFire.ts`,
  `src/utils/enemyShotPatterns.ts`, `src/utils/formations.ts`.
- **Difficulty scoring**: `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts` (absolute 0–100 index;
  movement/fire/health factors), pinned by
  `src/waves/enemyDifficulty.campaign.test.ts`.
- **Gym surface**: single reusable `GymEnemies` scene + `GymIndex`; new CSV rows
  appear automatically.
- **Precedent**: E6 Asteroid (AH-0MU8BZ2ZM004J47F) is already an arcade homage
  built as a non-formation roamer with a split helper — a model for how far a
  new archetype may depart from the formation model.
- GDD §8 "Future Scope" already anticipates "Levels 6–10+ with new enemy
  types".

## Desired change

Produce researched, ready-to-implement enemy concepts drawn from classic arcade
games and capture each as a scoped child work item, with a shared research
document acting as the catalogue and the record of deferred candidates.

**Proposed candidate pool** (research selects 5–8; the rest go in the
"considered but not selected" section):

- Space Invaders — marching row that steps left/right and drops bombs.
- Galaga — entrance dive-in formation and tractor/capture beam.
- Pac-Man — ghost chase with distinct pursue/ambush personalities.
- Centipede — segmented chain that descends and reacts on segment destruction.
- Defender — fast attacker with a defined patrol/attack run.
- Missile Command — incoming falling projectiles / orbital strike telegraphed.
- Robotron 2084 — aggressive horde that swarm-steers toward the player.
- Frogger — lane traffic hazard crossing the arena (non-shooting obstacle).
- Joust — flapping momentum-based flyer in the top-down arena.
- Dig Dug — burrower that creates/changes traversal hazards.
- Q*bert — diagonal hopper with a fixed stepping pattern.
- Star Castle — concentric rotating ring shielding a core.

*(Every candidate in the pool is recorded in the research document; only 5–8
become child work items.)*

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/CLASSIC_ENEMY_RESEARCH.md` — New. The catalogue of selected and
  deferred archetypes (the epic's primary deliverable).
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — Updated. Add a reference to the
  research doc; each implemented archetype later updates the catalog (§1) via
  its child item.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — Updated. Reference the research doc from
  §4.1 / §8 so the roster direction is traceable.
- `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` — Updated (by child items, not this epic). New
  rows for archetypes expressible as data.
- `src/entities/<Name>.ts` — New (by child items). Only for archetypes needing
  new entity code (e.g. burrower, segmented chain).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.ts` / new gym scene — Exercised by child items for
  parity.

## Related work

- **Enemy Design tooling** (AH-0MTFP7EIC004F1MN) — completed; the data-driven
  CSV pipeline new enemies plug into.
- **Asteroids as an enemy** (AH-0MU8BZ2ZM004J47F) — completed; precedent for a
  classic-arcade-inspired, non-formation enemy.
- **Enemy difficulty scoring** (AH-0MTZWZ7MC002B01K) — completed; every new
  archetype must supply its scoring inputs.
- **Extract common enemy base class for regular enemies** (AH-0MU4KQ6NT006MP52)
  — completed; the `BaseEnemy` seam new archetypes extend.
- **Data-driven enemy health config** (AH-0MUJRVYJH00485YR) — completed.
- **Docs and README for enemy config pipeline** (AH-0MTHG5K6O008BCNJ) —
  completed.
- **Write ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md best-practice guide**
  (AH-0MTAN4X5D009D7U6) — completed; the guide §8.6 governs each child.
- **Smart capture bot: survival-first heuristic** (AH-0MUX2NENC008AHOQ) —
  completed; automated playtests must survive any new enemy, so its behaviours
  are a useful validation input for selected archetypes.
- **Alternative player control** (AH-0MTF0EFNZ000RPVD) — completed.
- **Documentation: README, ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION, code comments**
  (AH-0MUE2MIXB007VOCY) — completed; docs-update conventions to follow.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUX2NENC008AHOQ** – Smart capture bot: survival-first heuristic that seeks power-ups and minerals and dodges fire patterns (completed)
- **AH-0MTF0EFNZ000RPVD** – Alternative player control (completed)
- **AH-0MUE2MIXB007VOCY** – Documentation: README, ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION, code comments (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: classic, create, drawn, dropping, eats (+23 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: arcade, classic, create, drawn, dropping (+23 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: create, enemies, epic, era, etc (+17 more)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk**: the research could expand indefinitely. Mitigation — cap
  selection at 5–8 this round; record all other candidates in the deferred
  section. Extra opportunities become linked work items, not scope.
- **Fidelity risk**: lane/axis-based arcade behaviours may need significant
  translation to the top-down free-2D arena; the brief requires each archetype
  to state its translation, and permits a documented divergence (per gym-parity
  rule).
- **Pipeline-fit risk**: some archetypes (burrower, segmented chain) cannot be
  expressed as a CSV row alone; the brief requires each to state whether a new
  entity/factory seam is needed before implementation starts.
- **Assumption**: the operator-supplied exemplars (Space Invaders row,
  Pac-Man ghosts, Centipede) are illustrative examples, not a required final
  selection.
- **Assumption**: "classic arcade era" means the coin-op era of the late 1970s
  to mid-1980s.
- **Assumption**: this epic's children implement the enemies; no separate
  implementation epic is needed.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 "How many enemy concepts should this epic research and turn into work
  items?" — Answer (operator): **(A) focused set of ~5–8** from a named
  shortlist of classics. Source: interactive reply. Research: reviewed
  `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §8.6 and the existing 7-archetype
  roster; a 5–8 cap keeps the epic tractable and each child implementable.
- Q2 "Should the epic also produce a written research/design document, or only
  the child work items?" — Answer (operator): **(B) a dedicated research doc
  plus child work items**, and *"be sure to include other candidates not
  selected but considered so we can expand the range later"*. Source:
  interactive reply. Research: `/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/intake` step 7
  and the repo's `docs/` convention; no existing research doc.
- Q3 "What should each per-enemy child work item include?" — Answer (operator):
  **(A) research + design + implementation of one enemy (full lifecycle in one
  child)**. Source: interactive reply.


---

## Plan

**Breakdown (created as child work items):** 1 research/validation child (R1)
+ 8 archetype full-lifecycle children (one per selected archetype) + 1
docs-integration child (D1). The epic itself does not implement the enemies.

**Selected archetypes (8):**

1. Space Invaders — stepping march formation.
2. Galaga — tractor/capture beam.
3. Pac-Man — ghost personalities (chase/ambush/flank/wander).
4. Centipede — segmented chain that splits on segment death.
5. Robotron 2084 — homing horde that swarm-steers to the player.
6. Defender — patrol-then-attack raider state machine.
7. Missile Command — telegraphed orbital strike.
8. Frogger — non-shooting lane traffic hazard.

**Considered but not selected (recorded in the research doc):** Joust, Dig Dug,
Q*bert, Star Castle.

**Test-first ordering:** R1 (research doc + automated engine-constraint
validation test) → E1–E8 (each a vertical slice: code + tests + code comments +
gym parity) → D1 (cross-cutting docs integration).

**Dependencies:** each archetype child depends on R1 (design brief must exist
before implementation); D1 depends on all archetype children (the GDD catalog
and guide must reflect the implemented roster).

**Phasing (vertical slices):** R1 is docs + validation test; each E* cuts
through the full layer stack (CSV/config → entity/factory/fire seam → shared
core → game + gym parity → tests → code comments); D1 is a cross-cutting docs
slice. Between phases, the next child's description is re-checked against what
was actually delivered and updated before implementation starts.

**Reused seams:** `BaseEnemy`, `EnemyConfig`/CSV pipeline
(`configStore`/`configCsvPlugin`), `formations.ts`, `enemyShotPatterns.ts`,
`enemyFire.ts` dispatcher, `AsteroidSpawner`/`HarvesterSpawner` (non-formation
spawner precedent), `GymEnemies`/`GymIndex`, `enemyDifficulty.ts`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers (planning)

- Q4 "When does the archetype selection get fixed?" — Answer (operator):
  **(A) fix the 5–8 selection now and create all children in this planning
  pass**. Source: interactive reply. Research: the epic's AC3 requires a child
  per selected archetype and the research doc's content is the same design
  brief, so fixing the set now avoids an extra planning pass and satisfies
  coverage immediately.
- Q5 "Which archetypes do you want selected?" — Answer (operator):
  **(A) select all 8 recommended** (Space Invaders, Galaga, Pac-Man,
  Centipede, Robotron 2084, Defender, Missile Command, Frogger); Joust, Dig
  Dug, Q*bert and Star Castle are deferred to the "considered but not selected"
  section. Source: interactive reply. Research: each selected archetype maps to
  a distinct existing/planned engine seam; the deferred four are weaker fits
  for a terrain-less top-down arena or overlap existing entities.
- Q6 "Breakdown shape for the children." — Answer (operator): **(A) a
  test/verification-first research-doc child (with an automated engine-
  constraint validation test) + one full-lifecycle child per selected
  archetype + a docs-integration child**. Source: interactive reply. Research:
  epic AC7 (README/GDD/guide) is cross-cutting and would otherwise be
  duplicated across 8 archetype children.
