# Add figure-of-8 boss movement in shared core

## Goal / user story

As a player, I want the boss to move in a figure-of-8 so the encounter is dynamic and I have to track my shots; as a developer I want the motion implemented once so `PlayScene` and every boss gym stay in parity.

This is part of parent Enhance Central AI boss encounter (AH-0MUY3X4NS007JR8X), covering parent AC3.

## Existing state

- `src/entities/Boss.ts`: `applyFormationPosition()` is a static `setPosition(baseX, baseY)`.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` `_advanceBoss(dt)` calls `boss.update(this.time.now, dt*1000, GAME_WIDTH, GAME_HEIGHT)` for **both** the game and `GymBoss` — the correct shared per-frame home for motion.
- `GymFormationScene` calls `entity.applyFormationPosition(baseX, baseY, dt, ...)` on its boss each tick.

## Desired change

1. In the shared boss core, trace a Gerono lemniscate (figure-8) about the boss's spawn **anchor**:
   `theta = 2*PI * elapsedMs / BOSS_MOVE_PERIOD_MS`, `x = anchorX + BOSS_MOVE_AMPLITUDE_X * sin(theta)`,
   `y = anchorY + BOSS_MOVE_AMPLITUDE_Y * sin(2*theta)`.
   Export `BOSS_MOVE_AMPLITUDE_X = 120`, `BOSS_MOVE_AMPLITUDE_Y = 60`, `BOSS_MOVE_PERIOD_MS = 8000`.
2. Accumulate motion time in `Boss.update(...)` (from `delta`) and set the boss position there, so both scenes get identical motion via `CombatScene._advanceBoss`.
3. Change `applyFormationPosition()` to set the **anchor** (not teleport the container), so the gym's per-frame call cannot fight the figure-8.
4. Clamp the traced position to the playfield bounds so the boss never leaves the screen.
5. Hit detection continues to use the boss's live `x`/`y`; the health bar does not move (delivered by the sibling health-bar task).

## Key Files

- `src/entities/Boss.ts` — motion constants, state, `update()`, `applyFormationPosition()`.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — confirm `_advanceBoss` drives motion for both scenes.
- `src/entities/Boss.test.ts` — traced-position and bounded-amplitude tests.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.test.ts` — gym motion parity.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — duplicate-body guard.

## Acceptance Criteria

- After a deterministic `delta`, the boss position follows the lemniscate about its anchor with peak amplitudes ≈120 px horizontal and ≈60 px vertical and a full cycle of ≈8 s.
- The boss x/y stay within the playfield bounds across a full cycle.
- Calling `applyFormationPosition(baseX, baseY, ...)` sets the anchor without overriding the live figure-8 position.
- The boss's live position is used for hit detection; the health bar's screen position is unchanged while the boss moves.
- Motion is implemented once in shared core (attributable to the sibling health-bar task that keeps the bar static).

**Parent AC traceability (mirrors parent AH-0MUY3X4NS007JR8X):**
- (parent AC3) **The boss moves in a figure-of-8 pattern.** The boss traces a lemniscate around its spawn anchor (≈120 px horizontal, ≈60 px vertical amplitude, ≈8 s per full cycle), staying within the playfield. Movement is implemented once in the shared boss/combat core and is identical in `PlayScene` and every boss gym. Hit detection continues to use the boss's live position, and the health bar does not move with it. Verified by tests asserting the traced position and bounded amplitude.
data.title: Add figure-of-8 boss movement in shared core

# Add dedicated boss-hit SFX cue

## Goal / user story

As a player, I want a distinct, punchy sound on every boss hit so hits feel responsive and obviously register.

This is part of parent Enhance Central AI boss encounter (AH-0MUY3X4NS007JR8X), covering the SFX half of parent AC5.

## Existing state

- `src/audio/effects.ts` exposes the boss cues (`playBossFireSound`, etc.) via the shared ToneForge playback layer.
- `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` maps every sound-producing cue to a recipe (baked/existing-recipe/runtime-shim) and seeds; `src/audio/cueManifest.ts` is the typed runtime view; `src/audio/cueManifest.test.ts` enforces completeness.
- Baked WAVs live in `public/audio/sfx/` and are **tracked in git**; recipes live in `audio/toneforge/recipes/`.

## Desired change

1. Add a new recipe `audio/toneforge/recipes/aihell-boss-hit.yaml` producing a short, punchy boss-hit impact (model the YAML shape on `aihell-boss-fire.yaml`).
2. Add a new baked manifest entry in `audio/toneforge/manifest.json`: `{ "cue": "playBossHitSound", "recipe": "aihell-boss-hit", "delivery": "baked", "seeds": [<new seed>] }`.
3. Add `playBossHitSound()` to `src/audio/effects.ts` (delegating to `playCue`).
4. Render and commit the baked WAV `public/audio/sfx/aihell-boss-hit.<seed>.wav` via the documented audio build pipeline (`scripts/build-audio.sh` / ToneForge).
5. Add/extend the cue-manifest contract test to require `playBossHitSound`.

## Key Files

- `audio/toneforge/recipes/aihell-boss-hit.yaml` (new).
- `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` — new cue entry + seed.
- `public/audio/sfx/aihell-boss-hit.<seed>.wav` (new, committed).
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — `playBossHitSound()`.
- `src/audio/cueManifest.ts`, `src/audio/cueManifest.test.ts` — mapping/contract.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `playBossHitSound` is exported from `src/audio/effects.ts` and appears in `CUE_MANIFEST` with recipe `aihell-boss-hit` and delivery `baked`.
- The recipe YAML exists, is valid, and the baked WAV for its seed is present under `public/audio/sfx/` and tracked.
- The cue-manifest contract test passes and fails if `playBossHitSound` is removed.
- No new runtime dependency is added.

# Add per-hit boss impact VFX on shared feedback path

## Goal / user story

As a player, I want an obvious impact flash at the point where my shot hits the boss — every single hit — so I can see and hear that my fire is connecting.

This is part of parent Enhance Central AI boss encounter (AH-0MUY3X4NS007JR8X), covering the VFX half of parent AC5.

## Existing state

- `src/vfx/bulletImpact.ts` provides `spawnBulletImpact(scene, x, y, options)` (used by `CombatScene` for non-lethal multi-hit enemy feedback on the Harvester) with `radius`/`duration`/`registry` options.
- `src/entities/Boss.ts` `takeDamage()` is the single shared point both `PlayScene._damageBoss()` and `GymBoss.damageBoss()` funnel through; it currently only plays the phase-transition cue on a depleting hit and gives no per-hit feedback.
- `PlayScene.onPlayerBulletHitsBoss` / `onAoeHitsBoss` know the hit point (`pb.x`/`pb.y`); `GymBoss.damageBoss()` damages at the boss centre.

## Desired change

1. Extend `spawnBulletImpact` with an optional `color` option (default unchanged) so boss hits can use a hot impact colour.
2. Change `Boss.takeDamage(hitX?, hitY?)` to play `playBossHitSound()` and spawn `spawnBulletImpact` at `(hitX ?? this.x, hitY ?? this.y)` on **every** landed hit. Retain the existing phase-transition cue on a depleting hit.
3. Track per-hit VFX in a small registry (`_hitEffects`) for test observability, removed on completion and torn down in `destroy()`.
4. Thread the hit point through `PlayScene._damageBoss(hitX?, hitY?)` from `onPlayerBulletHitsBoss`/`onAoeHitsBoss`; the gym calls `takeDamage()` at the boss centre.
5. Keep the feedback in the shared `Boss.takeDamage()` path so the game and gym cannot diverge.

## Key Files

- `src/entities/Boss.ts` — `takeDamage(hitX?, hitY?)`, hit VFX/SFX, registry, teardown.
- `src/vfx/bulletImpact.ts` — optional `color` option.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — thread hit point through `_damageBoss`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts` — gym uses the shared path.
- `src/entities/Boss.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.test.ts`, `src/vfx/bulletImpact.test.ts` — feedback tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every boss hit registers exactly one impact VFX at the supplied hit point (or the boss centre when none) and plays `playBossHitSound`.
- A depleting hit still plays the existing phase-transition cue in addition to the per-hit cue/VFX.
- Both `PlayScene` and `GymBoss` receive the same feedback because it lives in shared `Boss.takeDamage()`.
- The VFX registry is emptied on completion and on `destroy()` (no leak / no orphan Graphics).
- Tests assert an impact effect is registered per hit and at the expected coordinates.

**Parent AC traceability (mirrors parent AH-0MUY3X4NS007JR8X):**
- (parent AC5) **Hits on the boss are obvious with both SFX and VFX.** Every hit on the boss plays a dedicated boss-hit SFX cue and spawns an obvious impact VFX (flash/burst) at the hit point; phase transitions retain their existing distinct cue and visual. Game and gym use the same shared feedback path. Verified by the cue-manifest contract test (new cue registered) and VFX tests (an impact effect is registered per hit).
data.title: Add per-hit boss impact VFX on shared feedback path

# Implement on-screen action intensity metric (recording + video join)

**Sibling epic** of the research/decision item [Screen action intensity
tracking and analysis (AH-0MUZCSJXQ004TREN)] —
`discovered-from:AH-0MUZCSJXQ004TREN`. Created by that item's AC5. This is a
sibling (not a child) so the research item can close once its decision is
recorded without waiting for implementation.

## Goal

Implement the hybrid layered `actionIntensity` metric decided in
`docs/dev/action-intensity.md`: a pure, deterministic, O(entities) score of
on-screen presence + event bursts, recorded through the existing telemetry
pipeline, serialised as a versioned time series, and joinable to captured
WebM for highlight selection.

## User stories

- **As a game designer**, I can view a time-series of on-screen action
  intensity for a run, so I can evaluate pacing and find boring or
  over-crowded segments.
- **As a video editor**, I can map action-intensity peaks to captured-video
  timestamps and auto-select highlight clips.
- **As a maintainer**, the metric is computed once in the shared core and
  consumed identically by the game and the gyms, and reuses the telemetry
  pipeline rather than a parallel instrumentation path.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Pure core module.** A pure `computeActionIntensity(state, config)`
  lives in the shared core (`src/scenes/core/`), is O(entities) + O(1) per
  event, introduces no RNG, and returns the sample shape (rawScore,
  intensity, smoothed, burstiness, per-category breakdown) defined in the
  decision document §7.1. Unit-tested hermetically (no browser).
- **AC2 — Config.** All knobs (per-category weights incl. the refined
  player-bullet 0.5 and asteroids 1.0; `cap_c`; event window `W`; reference
  budget `B`; blend `k_E`; half-life `h`; sample rate) are config-driven with
  the decision-document defaults, and documented at the definition site.
- **AC3 — Telemetry integration.** The metric is wired into the per-tick
  telemetry `state` via the instrumentation child (AH-0MUY08VVQ007HSSH),
  reusing the `BotSnapshot` builder's registries. Recording is a **strict
  no-op when telemetry is disabled** (zero records, no allocation). No new
  schema bump is required (payload-only change); the shape is documented in
  `docs/TELEMETRY.md`.
- **AC4 — Event-window layer.** The burst layer consumes the discrete events
  the instrumentation child records (`enemy_killed`, `player_hit`,
  `boss_phase`, `powerup_collected`, `wave_clear`), with the documented
  default event values; verified by tests over a seeded event sequence.
- **AC5 — Derived time series.** A tooling-side serialiser emits the
  standalone JSONL artefact (`schemaVersion`, `runSeed`, `sampleRateHz`,
  `categories` header + one sample per line, `t` in ms since run start) to a
  git-ignored location alongside the capture output, with a matching
  basename. Round-trip tested.
- **AC6 — Video join + highlight selection.** A dev-gated `capture_started`
  marker (epoch ms, `import.meta.env.DEV`) is emitted at recording start; a
  helper maps `t` to video time using the shared anchor and returns merged
  highlight windows from the documented thresholds. Pure and unit-tested.
- **AC7 — Gym↔game parity.** The counter is authored once in the shared core
  and consumed by `PlayScene` and the gym scenes; the duplicate-body guard
  (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) still passes. A single
  count-able registry (or per-kind live counters) exists for enemy/boss
  explosion VFX so categories are not double-counted.
- **AC8 — Docs & tests.** `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` is cross-linked from
  `README.md` and `docs/TELEMETRY.md`; the full suite, typecheck and build
  pass; no shipped-bundle impact (`npm run check-bundle` passes).

## Dependencies

- **Epic AH-0MUY089KR003F8S4** — Realistic demo/attract bot framework +
  playtester telemetry (must be at least `high`; verified).
- **AH-0MUY08VJ9006BHJO** — Telemetry framework: versioned schema, pluggable
  sinks, consent flag (provides the envelope/sinks; completed).
- **AH-0MUY08VVQ007HSSH** — Game telemetry instrumentation: per-tick state and
  events (canonical integration point; `actionIntensity` field lives here).
- **AH-0MUWMFF3C002WOBK** — Automated gameplay capture spike (video consumer
  for the join).

Implementation must wait for AH-0MUY08VVQ007HSSH's tick-state integration
point to land (or land first if sequenced ahead of it).

## Key files (predicted)

- `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` — the decision this epic implements.
- `src/scenes/core/` — new pure `actionIntensity` module + config (+ tests).
- `src/ai/botSnapshot.ts` — existing registries the metric reads.
- `src/telemetry/` — recorder integration (via AH-0MUY08VVQ007HSSH);
  `docs/TELEMETRY.md` schema note.
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` / `scripts/capture-run-lifecycle.mjs` —
  `capture_started` marker + highlight-selection helper.
- `README.md` — cross-link to the decision document.

## Out of scope

- Driving pacing / adaptive difficulty from the metric (separate consumer
  work item).
- Calibration against human/physiological data (separate follow-up; required
  before the metric drives difficulty).
- ML excitement prediction and automatic editing.
data.title: Implement on-screen action intensity metric (recording + video join)

# Core: pure actionIntensity computation + config

Implements the pure `computeActionIntensity(state, config)` function and the full config object.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **AC1 — Pure core module.** A pure `computeActionIntensity(state, config)` implemented in the shared core and unit-tested hermetically.
- **AC2 — Config.** All knobs (per-category weights incl. the refined player-bullet and asteroid weights) are config-driven with documented defaults.
- **AC1a — Pure module (detail).** A `computeActionIntensity(state, config)` function lives in `src/scenes/core/actionIntensity.ts`, is O(entities) per tick, O(1) per event, introduces no RNG, and returns the sample shape: `{ rawScore, intensity, smoothed, burstiness, breakdown }` as defined in `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` §7.1.
- **AC2a — Config (detail).** All knobs are config-driven with defaults: per-category weights (player bullets 0.5, enemy bullets 1.0, enemies 2.0, asteroids 1.0, drops 1.0, enemy explosions 2.0, boss explosions 5.0, player explosions 20.0, bosses 5.0), `cap_c`, event window `W` (2.0 s), reference budget `B` (30), blend `k_E` (1.0), half-life `h` (0.5 s), sample rate (10 Hz). Defaults documented at definition site.

**Key Files:**
- `src/scenes/core/actionIntensity.ts` — new module
- `src/scenes/core/actionIntensity.test.ts` — unit tests

**Implementation:**
1. Define the config interface and default config object at the top of the module.
2. Implement `computeActionIntensity` as a pure function taking `(state: MinimalState, config: Config) => Sample`.
3. The state parameter needs: counts per category (playerBullets, enemyBullets, enemies, asteroids, drops, enemyExplosions, bossExplosions, playerExplosions, bosses) plus events since last sample.
4. Unit-test hermetically: construct state objects directly, no browser needed. Test presence layer, normalisation, smoothing, burstiness, per-category breakdown. Test config defaults.
5. Test edge cases: zero entities, pathological swarms (cap_c), empty events.

# Core: event-window burst layer

Implements the event-window burst layer that consumes discrete telemetry events.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **AC4 — Event-window layer.** The burst layer consumes the discrete events with documented default values over a seeded sequence.

**Key Files:**
- `src/scenes/core/actionIntensity.ts` — event-window functions (add to existing module)
- `src/scenes/core/actionIntensity.test.ts` — event sequence tests

**Implementation:**
1. Define the event types and their default values in the config module.
2. Implement the sliding window accumulator: `E(t) = Σ_{e : t-W < t_e ≤ t} v_e` where W=2.0s default.
3. Combine with presence layer: `R(t) = P(t) + k_E · E(t)` where k_E=1.0 default.
4. Unit-test over a seeded event sequence: verify window behaviour, event values, edge cases (events at window boundary, no events, burst of events).
5. Test the combined raw score R(t).

Maps action intensity timestamps to captured video and returns highlight windows.

**Key Files:**
- `scripts/capture-run-lifecycle.mjs` — add `capture_started` marker (dev-gated)

- `src/scenes/core/actionIntensityHighlights.ts` — pure highlight selection helper
- `src/scenes/core/actionIntensityHighlights.test.ts` — unit tests

**Implementation:**
1. Add a dev-gated `capture_started` epoch ms marker at the `MediaRecorder` start point in `capture-run-lifecycle.mjs`.
2. Create a pure helper: `mapTimeToVideo(t, capture_started, run_startedAt) => videoTimeMs`.
3. Create highlight window computation: read JSONL, find peak windows where `burstiness ≥ 0.15` and/or `intensity ≥ 0.7`, merge within 1.0s gap, apply lead (1.5s) / tail (1.0s).
4. All highlight logic is pure and unit-testable. No browser needed for tests.
5. Test: time mapping (with and without capture_started), highlight window detection, gap merging, boundary clamping (first sample may predate capture_started).
6. Gate all video-join code behind `import.meta.env.DEV`.

# Research catalogue and engine-constraint validation

Part of epic **Research classic enemies from the arcade games of old** (AH-0MUYAQ6YH0010G52).
This is the test/verification-first, primary research deliverable of the epic.

## User story

As the game designer, I want a single researched catalogue of the selected
classic arcade enemy archetypes (source, adaptation, pipeline fit, difficulty
inputs and gym scene) plus the deferred candidates, so the roster direction is
traceable and future expansion does not repeat the research.

## Required content

`docs/CLASSIC_ENEMY_RESEARCH.md` records, for each of the **8 selected**
archetypes (Space Invaders, Galaga, Pac-Man, Centipede, Robotron 2084,
Defender, Missile Command, Frogger): source game and era; original behaviour;
AI_Hell adaptation to the top-down free-2D neon-vector arena (including any
documented divergence); pipeline fit (`EnemyConfig`/CSV row vs a new
`src/entities/<Name>.ts` plus factory/fire-dispatch seam); difficulty scoring
inputs (movement / fire / health factors); gym scene(s) for parity; and
selection rationale.

A **"Considered but not selected"** section lists the remaining research-pool
candidates (Joust, Dig Dug, Q*bert, Star Castle) with a one-line deferral
reason each.

## Verification

A Vitest docs guard (`src/classicEnemyResearchDocs.test.ts`, matching the
`src/*Docs.test.ts` convention) asserts the research document exists, contains
5-8 selected archetypes, has the deferred section, and that each selected
archetype names a registry entry (existing or explicitly planned in its child
work item) and a gym scene. TDD: write the guard first, then make it pass.

## Key Files

- `docs/CLASSIC_ENEMY_RESEARCH.md` - New. The catalogue.
- `src/classicEnemyResearchDocs.test.ts` - New. Automated validation guard.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` - Updated. Reference the research doc.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The research document `docs/CLASSIC_ENEMY_RESEARCH.md` exists and catalogues at least 5 and at most 8 selected classic arcade enemy archetypes, recording for each its source game, original behaviour, adaptation to AI_Hell's neon-vector code-drawn no-enemy-collision rules, and why it was selected.
- The research document includes a "considered but not selected" section listing the remaining candidates from the research pool, each with a one-line reason for deferral, so the range can be expanded later.
- Each selected archetype's design notes specify its data-driven pipeline fit, i.e. whether it is expressible as an `EnemyConfig`/CSV row or needs a new `src/entities/<Name>.ts` plus factory/fire-dispatch seam, and its enemy difficulty scoring inputs (movement / fire / health factors).
- Each selected archetype's notes name the gym scene(s) that will exercise it (existing `GymEnemies` or a new gym) to satisfy the gym-to-game parity rule.

# Space Invaders marching formation

Part of epic **Research classic enemies from the arcade games of old** (AH-0MUYAQ6YH0010G52).
Design brief: `docs/CLASSIC_ENEMY_RESEARCH.md` (selected archetype: **Space Invaders**).
Implements one selected classic-arcade archetype as a full vertical slice
(config, entity, tests, code comments, gym parity).

## User story

As a player, I want a block of invaders that marches sideways, reverses at the arena edge, drops a row each time and speeds up as I thin it out, so that clearing the block feels like the classic escalating Space Invaders pressure.

## Source and adaptation

- **Source:** Space Invaders (Taito, 1978)
- **Original behaviour:** A block of aliens moves horizontally one step at a time; when the block reaches an edge it reverses and drops one row; one alien periodically drops a bomb; the block speeds up as members are destroyed.
- **AI_Hell adaptation:** The whole formation marches horizontally by a fixed step, reverses at the arena edge, and drops a fixed vertical step on each reversal, matching the original cadence. Bombs are ordinary AI_Hell aimed shots enabled only where the level's fire rule allows (Levels 4+; none in Levels 1-3). March speed scales up as the group thins, using the live alive count. Neon-vector code-drawn chevron/alien bodies; members pass through each other (no enemy-enemy collision).

## Pipeline fit

Likely a new `formationKind` (e.g. `march`) plus a couple of neutral config fields (step, drop) added to `EnemyConfig`/`ENEMY_COLUMN_ORDER` so the behaviour stays data-driven and editable in the gym panel. A new `src/entities/Invader.ts` is justified only if the step/reverse/drop cannot live in the shared formation movement policy. Either way the behaviour lives once in `src/scenes/core/`.

## Difficulty scoring inputs

`count`, `driftSpeed`, `formationKind` (new ordinal), `shotPattern` (none in L1-3; aimed/coordinated in L4+), `fireInterval`, `bulletSpeed`, `bulletLifetime`, `health` (1). The march speed-up is a derived behaviour, not a new factor.

## Gym parity

`GymEnemies` (existing) via its CSV row; the march, reversal, drop and speed-up are all visible and editable in the gym editor panel.

## Key Files

- `src/entities/Invader.ts` - New (only if a new entity is needed beyond the shared march policy).
- `src/utils/formations.ts` - Updated. March formation builder or movement policy registration.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` / `CombatScene.ts` - Updated. Shared march step/reverse/drop.
- `src/core/configTypes.ts` / `src/core/enemyConfig.ts` - Updated. March fields or formationKind.
- `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` - Updated. New row(s).
- `src/core/configDefaults.ts` - Updated. Seed fallback.
- `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts` / `src/entities/enemyFire.ts` - Updated. Factory + fire-dispatch wiring.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.ts` - Exercised for parity (no code change expected).

## Implementation plan (follows ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md section 8.6)

1. Tune the march in `GymEnemies` (step size, drop, reversal cadence, speed-up).
2. Add the neutral data fields or a new `formationKind` that represents a marching block, following the CSV-first convention.
3. Implement the march movement policy in the shared formation/cruise code (`src/scenes/core/` and/or `src/utils/formations.ts`) so game and gym share one implementation.
4. Wire any new archetype key through `enemyFactory.ts` and `enemyFire.ts` (non-firing entry where applicable).
5. Add a `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` row and a `DEFAULT_ENEMY_CONFIGS` seed fallback plus `health`.
6. Add unit/integration tests for step/reverse/drop/speed-up and parity; run the full suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

## User story

As a player, I want a set of pursuers each with its own personality - one that chases directly, one that ambushes ahead of me, one that flanks and one that wanders - alternating between scatter and chase, so that dodging them is about reading distinct behaviours rather than one homing blob.

## Source and adaptation

- **Source:** Pac-Man (Namco, 1980)
- **Original behaviour:** Four ghosts leave a central pen and pursue Pac-Man with distinct targeting rules (direct chase, ambush ahead, flank via a pivot, random wander), alternating scatter and chase phases on a timer.

A shared scatter/chase timer alternates their target modes. They pass through each other (no enemy-enemy collision), never shoot (enemies-are-the-bullets: body contact is lethal), and are worth points like other enemies.

## Pipeline fit

New entity plus a dynamic spawner, because the personalities are a steering behaviour no formation expresses. Data-driven via CSV rows (one row per personality or a new `personality` column); non-firing archetypes get an explicit `tryFireNone` entry so they never fall back to the aimed shot.

`count`, `driftSpeed` (pursuit speed), `formationKind` (`single`), `shotPattern` (`none`), `health` (1). Personalities are a steering variant, not a new scoring axis.

## User story

As a player, I want a telegraphed incoming strike that marks its impact point before a fast projectile falls and detonates, so I must keep moving and read the warning rather than react to an instantaneous hit.

## Source and adaptation

- **Source:** Missile Command (Atari, 1980)
- **Original behaviour:** Incoming missiles appear at the top of the screen and track down toward cities/ground, detonating on impact; the player intercepts them.
- **AI_Hell adaptation:** A target marker/warning appears at a predicted impact point near the player, holds for a configurable tell (at least 500 ms, matching the Phaser telegraph convention), then a fast projectile falls from off-screen and detonates in a radial burst at that point. This is a world hazard, not a wave-gating enemy ship: it does not count toward wave completion (same non-blocking accounting as asteroids), and it respects no enemy-enemy collision.

## Pipeline fit

New hazard entity plus a dynamic spawner (the asteroid precedent), and possibly a new `EnemyShotPattern` (`strike`) for the telegraph+radial burst. Data-driven via CSV columns.

## Difficulty scoring inputs

`count`, `shotPattern` (new strike/radial), `bulletSpeed`, `bulletLifetime`, `burstCount`, `fireInterval` (strike cadence), `health` (1).

## Gym parity

- `src/waves/StrikeSpawner.ts` - New. Non-blocking dynamic hazard spawner.
- `src/utils/enemyShotPatterns.ts` - Updated. Strike/telegraph pattern registration (if adopted).

2. Add a strike entity/projectile (`src/entities/OrbitalStrike.ts`) with the standard seam, plus a telegraph marker reusing the existing tell/advance-cue convention.

5. Unit-test the tell duration (>= 500 ms), impact point selection, blast pattern and non-blocking accounting; parity-test the shared path.
6. Run the full suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- This work item is the per-selected-archetype child for Missile Command: it contains a user story, measurable/testable acceptance criteria including unit tests, predicted key files, and an implementation plan following section 8.6 "Adding a new enemy" in `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, and references the epic AH-0MUYAQ6YH0010G52 and `docs/CLASSIC_ENEMY_RESEARCH.md`.
- The archetype's design notes specify how it fits the data-driven pipeline, i.e. whether it is expressible as an `EnemyConfig`/CSV row or needs a new `src/entities/<Name>.ts` plus factory/fire-dispatch seam, and give its enemy difficulty scoring inputs (movement / fire / health factors).
- The archetype's notes name the gym scene(s) that exercise it (existing `GymEnemies` or a new gym) for gym-to-game parity, and the implemented behaviour runs the same shared code in the gym and the game (enforced by `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`).
- A strike telegraphs its impact point with a visible marker for a configurable tell of at least 500 ms before the projectile falls; the tell duration is asserted by a unit test.
- The projectile falls to the telegraphed impact point and detonates in a radial burst; the impact position and blast pattern are unit-tested.
- The strike is a non-blocking hazard: it is not registered with wave completion (matching the asteroid accounting), verified by a test so a wave cannot stall or clear early.
- The detonation can damage the player (enemy-body/projectile death rule) but never collides with or damages other enemies, verified by tests.
- Unit and integration tests exist for the archetype's movement, firing/telegraphing (if any) and wave accounting; every acceptance criterion is covered by an automated test.
- Full project test suite passes with the new archetype and all new tests.

# Frogger lane traffic hazard

Part of epic **Research classic enemies from the arcade games of old** (AH-0MUYAQ6YH0010G52).
Design brief: `docs/CLASSIC_ENEMY_RESEARCH.md` (selected archetype: **Frogger**).
Implements one selected classic-arcade archetype as a full vertical slice
(config, entity, tests, code comments, gym parity).

## User story

As a player, I want lanes of fast traffic crossing the arena that I must weave through or shoot, so the arena has a moving spatial hazard distinct from homing enemies.

## Source and adaptation

- **Source:** Frogger (Konami/Sega, 1981)
- **Original behaviour:** Lanes of cars/logs cross the screen at constant speed; a collision with a car is fatal and the player must time crossings.
- **AI_Hell adaptation:** One to three traffic lanes cross the arena at constant speed and wrap at the edges; the hazards never fire and do not home. They are destructible (one player bullet each) to fit the enemies-are-the-bullets design and the asteroid/obstacle model, and they are non-blocking for wave completion (the asteroid accounting). They pass through each other and other enemies (no enemy-enemy collision).

## Pipeline fit

New hazard entity plus a dynamic spawner (asteroid precedent), or a reuse of the existing obstacle entity if its seam covers wrapping lanes. Data-driven via CSV columns; non-blocking wave accounting.

## Difficulty scoring inputs

`count` (per lane), `driftSpeed` (lane speed), `formationKind` (`single`/`rect`), `shotPattern` (`none`), `health` (1).

## Gym parity

`GymEnemies` (live player) for lane hazards; `GymLevel` may exercise them in a wave context. Shared core keeps parity.

## Key Files

- `src/entities/Traffic.ts` - New (or reuse/extend `src/entities/Obstacle.ts`). Lane hazard.
- `src/waves/TrafficSpawner.ts` - New. Non-blocking dynamic spawner.
- `src/core/configTypes.ts` / `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` - Updated. Lane fields and row.
- `src/core/configDefaults.ts` - Updated. Seed fallback.
- `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts` / `src/entities/enemyFire.ts` - Updated. Factory + `tryFireNone`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.ts` - Exercised for parity (or `GymLevel`).

## Implementation plan (follows ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md section 8.6)

1. Tune lane count, lane position, speed, spacing and wrap in a gym with a live player.
2. Add `src/entities/Traffic.ts` (or reuse/extend the existing obstacle entity) with the standard seam.
3. Add `src/waves/TrafficSpawner.ts` (modelled on `AsteroidSpawner`) with non-blocking wave accounting.
4. Add config/CSV fields (lane, speed, spacing) and seed fallbacks; register factory/fire-dispatch (`tryFireNone`).
5. Unit-test constant-speed motion, edge wrap, spacing, destructibility and non-blocking accounting; parity-test the shared path.
6. Run the full suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- This work item is the per-selected-archetype child for Frogger: it contains a user story, measurable/testable acceptance criteria including unit tests, predicted key files, and an implementation plan following section 8.6 "Adding a new enemy" in `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, and references the epic AH-0MUYAQ6YH0010G52 and `docs/CLASSIC_ENEMY_RESEARCH.md`.
- The archetype's design notes specify how it fits the data-driven pipeline, i.e. whether it is expressible as an `EnemyConfig`/CSV row or needs a new `src/entities/<Name>.ts` plus factory/fire-dispatch seam, and give its enemy difficulty scoring inputs (movement / fire / health factors).
- The archetype's notes name the gym scene(s) that exercise it (existing `GymEnemies` or a new gym) for gym-to-game parity, and the implemented behaviour runs the same shared code in the gym and the game (enforced by `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`).
- One or more traffic lanes cross the arena at constant speed and wrap at the edges; the motion and wrap are unit-tested.
- Traffic hazards never fire and are destructible by a single player bullet (1 HP); both are verified by tests.
- Traffic is a non-blocking hazard: it is not registered with wave completion (asteroid accounting), verified by a test.
- Traffic hazards pass through each other and other enemies (no enemy-enemy collision), verified by a test.
- Unit and integration tests exist for the archetype's movement, firing/telegraphing (if any) and wave accounting; every acceptance criterion is covered by an automated test.
- Full project test suite passes with the new archetype and all new tests.

# Intake Brief — Explosions timed with the beat (AH-0MV01HNLU008S5E3)

**Headline:** Player auto-fire already lands on a silent 80 BPM beat grid, but
non-weapon explosion SFX still fire on the exact death frame; schedule the
enemy/Diver/player destruction cues onto the next 16th note of the current
tempo so kills land rhythmically, while weapon cues keep their own
beat-synchronised firing pattern.

## Problem statement

`src/utils/beat.ts` already quantises every player weapon's fire to a silent,
configurable 80 BPM grid (AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B), so shots are rhythmically
regular. The explosion sounds for a destroyed enemy, Diver or the player are
still dispatched immediately from the kill frame, so the soundscape lands at
arbitrary offsets against the fire grid. The producer wants explosion SFX
deferred to the next 16th note of the current tempo, giving kills a rhythmic
accent without changing what the player sees.

## Users

- **Player:** hears kills land on the beat, reinforcing the game's pulse and
  making combat feel more musical.
- **Developer / designer tuning feel:** can adjust the quantisation (16th note,
  tempo/BPM) and the per-tick audio cap through existing config/constants in
  one place, with tests guarding the timing contract.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, when I destroy an enemy the boom lands on the next 16th note
  of the current tempo, so a burst of kills reads as a rhythmic accent rather
  than random noise.
- As a **player**, my ship's destruction sound is beat-aligned too, but nothing
  about the explosion is delayed visually — I still see the kill instantly.
- As a **developer**, I can change the tempo through the existing rules config
  (`beatBpm`) and the explosion schedule follows it automatically, in both the
  game and every gym.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — 16th-note delay helper:** A pure helper derives the delay to the next
  16th note from the shared beat clock — 16th note = `beatPeriodMs(bpm) / 4`
  (187.5 ms at the default 80 BPM) — returning `0` when the request is already
  on a tick and a finite value for an invalid/zero/negative tempo (falling back
  to `DEFAULT_BPM`, never a negative delay). Unit-tested.
- **AC2 — Non-weapon explosion cues quantised:** `playDestructionSound`
  (enemy/asteroid), `playDiverDestructionSound` and
  `playPlayerDestructionSound` are scheduled onto the next 16th note via the
  shared playback `delay` option. For a request at game-time `t`, the scheduled
  audio delay equals `next16th(t) - t` (asserted with a recording provider /
  spy).
- **AC3 — Weapon and interception cues unchanged:** The Mortar detonation cue
  and the Nova/Mortar/Arc fire cues keep firing immediately (weapons already
  fire on exact beat subdivisions), and `playBulletDestructionSound` stays
  immediate. A test asserts no beat delay is applied to these cues.
- **AC4 — Accent with a per-tick cap:** Several explosions requested inside one
  16th-note window all land on that same tick (one rhythmic accent), bounded by
  a small per-tick limiter/cap (tunable constant) so a mass kill cannot clip
  the mix. Both the accent and the cap are unit-tested.
- **AC5 — Audio-only and gym↔game parity:** Particle bursts, AOE detonation
  graphics and camera juice still spawn on the death frame — only the cue is
  deferred. The quantisation is implemented **once** in the shared core/audio
  seam and consumed by `PlayScene` and every gym; the
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` duplicate-body guard passes
  with no divergent copy.
- **AC6 — Pause/reset/tempo safety:** A frozen scene (beat clock not advanced)
  requests no cues and leaks no scheduled audio; a scene restart
  (`beatClock.reset()`) re-derives the schedule after the grid returns to
  origin; an invalid tempo still produces a valid, bounded delay.
- **AC7 — Testing/validation coverage:** New or extended tests exercise the
  helper maths (on-tick clamp, mid-window snap, invalid tempo), the scheduled
  delay for each in-scope cue, the weapon/interception exclusions, the per-tick
  cap and the VFX-unchanged path.
- **AC8 — Documentation:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
  changes, including code comments and the relevant GDD/audio docs
  (`docs/Game Design Document.md` §7.3/§4, `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`
  where the cue behaviour is described). (CHANGELOG.md is out of scope — owned
  by the ship release pipeline.)
- **AC9 — Full suite:** Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **The beat stays silent:** no audible metronome and no background music
  (GDD §7.3); this changes cue *timing* only.
- **Game-time vs audio-clock:** the beat clock is anchored in game time, while
  playback schedules against `AudioContext.currentTime`. The delay must be
  derived from the game-time distance to the tick (`nextTick − now`), not a
  wall-clock read.
- **No new audio context:** reuse the existing shared provider/playback layer;
  every cue still degrades to a safe no-op in headless tests (no `AudioContext`
  never throws).
- **Gym↔game parity:** the behaviour lives once in the shared core/audio seam
  (`src/scenes/core/`, `src/audio/effects.ts`, `src/utils/beat.ts`) and is
  consumed unchanged by `PlayScene` and every `src/scenes/gym/` scene
  (`AGENTS.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §5.1).
- **UK English** in all comments and documentation.

## Existing state

- `src/utils/beat.ts` — pure, configurable beat module: `beatPeriodMs(bpm)`,
  `beatSubdivisionMs(subdivisions, bpm)`, `nextTick`, `shotTimeFor`,
  `isOnGrid`, and `createBeatClock({ bpm, anchorMs })`. Default `80 BPM`
  (750 ms/beat). A 16th note is therefore `750 / 4 = 187.5 ms`.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — owns the single `beatClock` (created
  from `loadRules().beatBpm`), exposed via `getBeatClock()`; advanced only
  through `_autoFire`/`Player.tryFire`, so a paused scene pauses the clock.
- `src/audio/sfxPlayback.ts` — `SfxPlayOptions.delay` (seconds from
  `context.currentTime`) is already honoured by `play()`.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — `playCue(cue, options)` is the single dispatch; the
  destruction cues currently pass **no** delay:
  `playDestructionSound()`, `playDiverDestructionSound()`,
  `playPlayerDestructionSound(volumeScale)`.
- Kill seams that play those cues: `CombatScene.finaliseEnemyKill()`
  (generic/diver via `enemy.playDestructionAudio?()`), `PlayScene`'s
  `playDestructionAudio()` seam and direct calls, `GymFormationScene`, and
  `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts` (`playPlayerDestructionSound`).
- Precedent for scheduled explosion cues already exists: the victory fireworks
  (`playVictoryExplosionSound({ delay, volume })`) schedule each cue against its
  visual burst in `src/vfx/endOfRunJuice.ts`.

## Desired change

1. Add a pure helper (in `src/utils/beat.ts` or the audio layer) that returns
   the milliseconds/seconds to the next 16th-note tick for the current tempo.
2. Thread the scene's shared beat clock into the non-weapon explosion cue
   dispatch so the delay is passed through the existing `SfxPlayOptions.delay`
   channel — implemented once in the shared core/audio seam so the game and
   every gym behave identically.
3. Add a small per-tick cap for simultaneously-queued explosion cues.
4. Keep every weapon cue, the bullet-interception cue and all explosion VFX
   immediate.
5. Update the relevant docs and code comments.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/utils/beat.ts` — Add the 16th-note delay helper (and/or a shared
  `nextSubdivisionDelayMs`), with JSDoc and edge-case handling.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — Accept/derive a beat delay for the in-scope
  destruction cues; add the per-tick cap.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — Pass the beat-clock-derived delay at
  `finaliseEnemyKill()` (the shared kill seam), keeping parity.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — Expose/consume the shared beat clock
  for the audio schedule.
- `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts` — Route the player-death cue through the shared
  beat-aware dispatch (called by `PlayScene` / `GymFormationScene`).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — Update the destruction-audio call sites if the
  delay must be supplied by the caller.
- `src/audio/cueManifest.ts` / `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` — Only if
  the cue behaviour description changes (no new recipes expected).
- Tests: `src/utils/beat.test.ts`, `src/audio/effects.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` and the scene/gym audio
  tests.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption A1 — scope ("everything except weapons"):** quantise the
  non-weapon destruction booms (`playDestructionSound`,
  `playDiverDestructionSound`, `playPlayerDestructionSound`). Weapon cues
  (Mortar detonation, Nova/Mortar/Arc fire) are excluded because weapons
  already fire on exact beat subdivisions. `playBulletDestructionSound`
  (interception feedback) is also excluded.
- **Assumption A2 — victory fireworks out of scope:** the end-of-run victory
  explosions already schedule their cues explicitly against their visual
  bursts (`spawnVictoryFireworks`); adding a 16th-note quantisation would
  desync audio from those visuals. Treated as out of scope; recorded for
  producer confirmation.
- **Assumption A3 — swarm burst out of scope:** `playSwarmBurstSound` is an
  enemy-volley whoosh, not an explosion; left unchanged.
- **Risk R1 — audio/game clock skew:** if the audio context is suspended or the
  scene is paused, a fixed game-time delay could land late on resume. Mitigation:
  schedule from the game-time delta, clamp the maximum delay to one 16th note,
  and assert the no-cue-when-frozen path.
- **Risk R2 — clipping from stacked accents:** a mass kill can queue many cues
  onto one tick. Mitigation: the AC4 per-tick cap (documented, tested,
  tunable).
- **Risk R3 — parity drift:** computing the delay at only one call site would
  leave the game/gym behaviour divergent and trip the duplicate-body guard.
  Mitigation: one shared seam, enforced by AC5.
- **Risk R4 — scope creep:** applying the same treatment to enemy fire cues or
  other SFX is out of scope; record any such opportunity as a linked
  `discovered-from:` work item rather than folding it in.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUZQ33GR006AKXD** – Core: pure actionIntensity computation + config (completed)
- **AH-0MUWYQRML000FLMT** – Document audio capture and costs (completed)
- **AH-0MUGY8HHU006XMU9** – Run full test suite and fix any failures (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: beat, called, current, delay, explosion (+10 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: beat, called, current, delay, explosion (+10 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: called, current, explosion, land, next (+5 more)

**Manual cross-references**

- **AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B** — "Bullets from the players ship should always fall on
  the beat" (completed): the silent 80 BPM fire grid this item builds on; the
  beat clock in `src/utils/beat.ts` and `CombatCoreScene.beatClock` are its
  outputs.
- **AH-0MUGPSOVM006Z1OJ** — "Implement pure, configurable 80 BPM beat clock
  module" (completed): the helper this change extends.
- **AH-0MUGY84L1004H2UP** — "Make BPM and per-weapon subdivisions configurable
  via existing config plumbing" (completed): `beatBpm` in `src/core/rules.ts`
  is the tempo source the delay must follow.
- **AH-0MUGQCMNA0061J4A** — "Replace Player.tryFire per-weapon cooldowns with
  phase-locked beat scheduling" (completed): the phase-lock precedent.
- **AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V** — "Add particle-based explosion VFX for enemy and
  player deaths" (completed): the visual explosion layer deliberately left
  immediate by this item (Assumption A2/Q2=A).
- **AH-0MUJS85X0006EXGV** — "Major-explosion voice limiter" (completed):
  prior art for capping stacked explosion audio (AC4).
- **AH-0MUDY2ID7006VY3A** — "Dedicated player-destruction SFX" (completed):
  owns `playPlayerDestructionSound`, one of the in-scope cues.
- **AH-0MTVYC6E8005YN6F** — "Divers need SFX" (completed) and
  **AH-0MTCO1LGD0082SVG** — "Diver has no audio" (completed): own
  `playDiverDestructionSound`, another in-scope cue.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Which explosion cues are quantised to the next 16th note?** —
  Answer (operator, interactive reply): "Everything except weapons, which have
  their own synchronization pattern." → Scope is the non-weapon destruction
  booms: `playDestructionSound`, `playDiverDestructionSound`,
  `playPlayerDestructionSound`. Weapon cues (Mortar detonation, Nova/Mortar/Arc
  fire) stay immediate because the weapon fire grid already synchronises them.
- **Q2 — Do the visual explosions move with the audio, or only the sound?** —
  Answer (operator, interactive reply): "A" → Audio only; all explosion VFX
  (particle bursts, AOE detonation graphics, camera juice) stays on the death
  frame.
- **Q3 — How should several explosions requested inside one 16th-note window
  behave?** — Answer (operator, interactive reply): "A" → Accent/stack: every
  queued cue lands on the same next tick, with a small per-tick limiter/cap to
  protect the mix.
- **Assumption A2 (recorded, not a question):** victory-firework explosions are
  out of scope because they already schedule against their visual bursts.
- **Assumption A3 (recorded, not a question):** `playSwarmBurstSound` is a
  volley cue, not an explosion, and is left unchanged.

# AI Bot prioritises lives — intake brief

## Problem statement

The attract/demo bot (`createCompetentBotBrain`, driven by `PlayScene` in demo
mode) treats **Extra Life** as just another power-up. It therefore ignores the
single most valuable outcome in the run — preserving the ship — when a life is
under-capped, and it never steers deliberately toward an Extra Life drop on the
screen. When the hold-full choice opens, the bot auto-selects the **first**
option regardless of what is offered, so an offered Extra Life is frequently
passed over.

## Users

- **Player / operator watching attract mode** — wants the demo bot to play
  credibly, i.e. to value survival and to pick up lives when it can.

User stories:

- As a player watching attract mode, I want the demo bot to take an Extra Life
  offer in the hold-full selection when it is below the life cap, so the demo
  looks like a competent player.
- As a player watching attract mode, I want the demo bot to divert to an Extra
  Life drop that is on screen when it is below the life cap, so it does not
  squander a free life.

## Users / stakeholders

- **AI Bot** (the demo/attract bot) is the actor whose behaviour changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Hold-full choice prefers Extra Life.** When the hold-full choice
  offers `extra_life` and the bot's lives are below the cap (`5`), the bot
  selects the `extra_life` option (demo mode). When `extra_life` is not offered,
  or lives are at the cap, the existing auto-select behaviour is unchanged.
- **AC2 — On-screen Extra Life is prioritised.** While a live `extra_life` drop
  is on screen and the bot's lives are below the cap, the bot's chosen target is
  that drop (subject to the survival tier — the bot never trades its life for a
  life). At the life cap the drop receives no special priority.
- **AC3 — Life cap is single-sourced.** The life status used by the bot
  (`lives`, cap) is derived from the existing game data (GDD cap `5`,
  `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE.extra_life.livesMax`); no new magic `5` is introduced.
- **AC4 — Gym↔game parity preserved.** The change lives in shared code
  (snapshot/world/model/goal content or shared choice policy) and the
  duplicate-body guard (`CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) and gym-parity docs
  assertions still pass; any gym that exercises drop collection or the
  hold-full choice sees the same behaviour.
- **AC5 — Test coverage.** Unit tests cover: (a) the choice policy selects
  `extra_life` when offered and lives < cap, and falls back otherwise;
  (b) the drop-target priority puts an on-screen `extra_life` first when
  lives < cap and does not when at the cap; (c) survival still dominates the
  life preference.
- **AC6 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
  changes, including code comments, `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md`, and the GDD
  attract/demo subsection where it describes bot priorities.
- **AC7 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes** (typecheck,
  lint and build included).

## Constraints

- The demo bot is the shipped AI Bot; behaviour is only observable in demo
  mode, so the change must not alter normal (human) play, including the
  non-demo hold-full selection which must keep waiting for a real selection.
- Survival is a hard constraint above every other tier — the life preference
  is only ever applied when the bot can safely take it.
- Keep the 5-life cap consistent with the GDD (§3.1 / §4.5) and the Extra Life
  catalogue entry.
- No new magic numbers outside the existing bot tunables module(s).

## Existing state

- Demo bot: `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` → `botBrain = createCompetentBotBrain()`,
  decisions from `buildBotSnapshot(this)` (`src/ai/botSnapshot.ts`).
- `BotSnapshot` currently has **no life state** — `lives` is not exposed, so the
  decision layer cannot see the life count today.
- Priority bands (`src/ai/framework/competent/goals.ts`): survival >
  minerals > power-ups > enemies > asteroids. `extra_life` already has the
  highest power-up value (`1.5`, `src/ai/framework/competent/content.ts`), but
  minerals are a higher band, so minerals currently outrank an Extra Life drop.
- Hold-full choice: `PlayScene.openMineralChoice()` launches
  `MineralChoiceScene` with `options`; in demo mode it passes
  `autoSelectMs = BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS`, and the overlay then does
  `this.select(0)` — always the first option (`src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts`).
- Cap constants: `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE.extra_life.livesMax = 5`
  (`src/powerups/types.ts`); GDD §4.5 caps lives at 5.

## Desired change

1. Expose the bot's life state on `BotSnapshot` (lives + cap, or a derived
   `livesBelowCap` boolean) via `buildBotSnapshot`, read from the scene's run
   state.
2. Add a **secure-life** behaviour to the competent bot that targets a live
   `extra_life` drop when lives < cap, placed as the highest band below
   survival (above minerals). At the cap, the drop falls back to its existing
   power-up band.
3. In demo mode, make the hold-full auto-selection prefer the `extra_life`
   option when offered and lives < cap, otherwise keep the existing
   first-option behaviour.
4. Update docs and tests as above.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ai/botSnapshot.ts` — Add life state (`lives`, cap / `livesBelowCap`) to
  `BotSnapshot`, read from the scene's run state.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/goals.ts` — Add the `secure-life` priority band
  below survival and above minerals; keep content-adaptive registration.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/behaviours.ts` — Collect behaviour reuse for the
  life target.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/content.ts` — Reference the Extra Life cap /
  fallback value.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts` — Any new tunable (single source).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — Pass bot life state into the snapshot; choose the
  preferred demo option for the hold-full choice.
- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` — Accept a preferred demo selection index
  (instead of hard-coded `0`).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — Only if the choice/collection path is
  shared there (parity).
- `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md` — Document the life
  priority.
- Tests: `src/ai/framework/competent/*.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/__tests__/MineralChoiceScene.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** The life cap is `5` (GDD / `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE.extra_life.livesMax`).
- **Assumption:** The change targets the demo/attract bot (`PlayScene` demo
  mode). Normal player selection is never auto-driven.
- **Assumption:** "Prioritise lives" means Extra Life outranks minerals and all
  other power-ups when it can be safely taken and lives < cap. If the operator
  intended a weaker preference (Extra Life above other power-ups but below
  minerals), revisit AC1/AC2.
- **Assumption:** At the life cap the Extra Life drop receives no special
  attention (collecting it is wasted).
- **Risk — survival regression:** diverting to a life must not bypass the
  survival tier. Mitigated by keeping the new band strictly below survival.
- **Risk — parity drift:** bot/choice logic duplicated between game and gym
  would trip the duplicate-body guard. Mitigated by placing logic in shared
  core/competent modules.
- **Risk — scope creep:** "make the bot better at survival generally" is out of
  scope; record any such ideas as linked work items.
- **Assumption:** The legacy `botDecision.ts` heuristic is not the live demo
  brain (`PlayScene` uses the competent brain); if it is still consumed
  elsewhere, mirror the life preference there for consistency.

## Related work

- AH-0MUXXQ1MN002RXGB — Demo bot: human-like input limits and complete the
  hold-full upgrade choice (added the demo auto-select; this extends it).
- AH-0MUXYOV4C008MV0L — Demo bot movement goals: minerals > power-ups >

- AH-0MUY089KR003F8S4 — Realistic demo/attract bot framework + playtester

- AH-0MUNS3VAQ0023L1J — Increase the probability of lives powerup being spawned.

- `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` — competent bot goals/behaviours and priority bands.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §3.1 / §4.5 — lives model and cap.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should an on-screen Extra Life outrank minerals, or only other power-ups,
  when the bot has fewer than 5 lives?" — Answer (intake agent, documented
  assumption; seed intent "prioritize lives" read as strongest non-survival
  priority): "Outrank minerals when lives < cap; ignore at cap." Source: seed
  intent `AH-0MV03GXZQ00801T4`. **OPEN QUESTION** for producer: confirm this

- Q: "What is the life cap?" — Answer: `5`, from the GDD §4.5 and

- Q: "Does this affect human play?" — Answer: "No; the auto-selection change is

# Single enemy gym scene with in-panel enemy selector dropdown

## Problem statement

The dev gym index currently renders **one ENEMIES row per `EnemyConfig`**, each
booting the same reusable `GymEnemies` scene with a fixed `{ enemyKey }`. To
compare archetypes a designer must return to the index, and the column grows
with every "Save As…" entry. There is no way to switch the active enemy type
from inside the scene. We want **one** enemy gym scene with an in-panel
dropdown that swaps the active enemy type live.

## Users

- **Game designer / developer tuning enemy formations, shots and visuals.**
  - As a designer, I want a single enemy gym scene where I can pick any
    (non-boss) enemy from a dropdown, so that I can switch archetypes in one
    place without going back to the index.
  - As a designer, I want choosing an enemy to immediately clear the scene and
    spawn that enemy type, so that what I see always matches the selection.
  - As a designer, I want enemies I have created with "Save As…" to appear in
    the dropdown automatically, so new archetypes are testable with no code
    change.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.ts` is **already the single reusable enemy gym
  scene**: `GymEnemies extends GymFormationScene`, parameterised by
  `init(data?: { enemyKey?: string })`, with the plain-DOM "AI Config" panel
  (sliders, colour inputs, `formationKind`/`shotPattern` selects,
  Respawn/Player toggle, Save/Save As). It is registered under scene key
  `GymEnemies`.
- `src/scenes/GymIndex.ts` renders four columns:
  - left — plain scenes;
  - **ENEMIES** — one row per non-boss `EnemyConfig` via
    `discoverEnemyGymEntries()` (`src/utils/enemyGymDiscovery.ts`), each row
    `scene.start('GymEnemies', { enemyKey })`;
  - **Bosses** — "Boss Swarm" (the `boss` config, routed to `GymEnemies` via
    `enemyKey`) and "Boss" (the dedicated multi-phase `GymBoss` scene, booted
    directly via `sceneKey`);
  - **Dev Utilities** — tooling scenes (e.g. `GymCurveSequencer`).
- No enemy-type selector exists in the panel today.
- Seed configs: `scout diver tank phaser swarm boss asteroid harvester march
  capturer ghost-chase ghost-ambush ghost-flank ghost-wander grunt raider`
  (`src/data/enemy-configs.csv`), plus any user "Save As…" entries in storage.

## Desired change

1. **Rename the single enemy gym scene** `GymEnemies` →
   **`GymFodderEnemies`** (class, file `src/scenes/gym/GymFodderEnemies.ts`,
   scene key `GymFodderEnemies`, and every string/import reference), keeping
   its existing behaviour and panel. The name signals that this scene is the
   *fodder* (non-boss) enemy gym.
2. **Add an enemy selector dropdown** to the AI Config panel — a single
   `<select>` listing every **non-boss** `EnemyConfig`, resolved dynamically
   from the config store (`loadAllEnemyConfigs()` / `listEnemyConfigKeys()`) so
   seed and "Save As…" entries both appear. The selection is seeded from the
   scene's active enemy key. `boss` is deliberately **excluded** (the boss has
   its own entry — see 3).
3. **Rebuild the scene on selection change** (the core requirement):
   destroy every live formation entity and any player bullets, load the
   selected `EnemyConfig`, rebuild the formation config / entity factory /
   bullet dispatch, **reload every other panel control** from the selected
   config (discarding unsaved edits from the previous enemy), and spawn the
   new formation through the shared clean-slate seam
   (`GymFormationScene.respawnFormation()`), i.e. the same path the existing
   **Respawn** button already uses.
4. **Simplify the index to match:**
   - the ENEMIES column becomes a **single "Fodder Enemies" row** that boots
     `GymFodderEnemies` bare (dropdown default = `scout`); the per-config
     fodder rows are removed;
   - the **Bosses column and its header are removed**, and the dedicated
     **`GymBoss` "Boss" row is relocated into the ENEMIES column** (the
     redundant "Boss Swarm" `boss`-config row is dropped);
   - keyboard focus order (Tab/arrows/Enter) and ESC-to-menu continue to work
     across the revised layout.
5. Preserve the existing wave-timeout semantics (non-boss keys get the shared
   wave timeout; the `boss` key remains timeout-free) and all gym↔game parity
   conventions — reuse the shared core seams, do not fork gameplay code.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Rename** `GymEnemies` → `GymFodderEnemies`: `src/scenes/gym/GymFodderEnemies.ts`
      exports `GymFodderEnemies` registered under scene key `GymFodderEnemies`;
      no production code routes to or imports a scene key/class named
      `GymEnemies` (historical documentation notes may retain the old name with
      a "formerly" note).
- [ ] **Dropdown present and dynamic**: the AI Config panel renders exactly one
      enemy `<select>` whose options are the non-boss config keys (seed +
      storage), including a newly "Save As…" key after re-boot, with the active
      key selected; no hard-coded key list.
- [ ] **Selection change rebuilds the scene**: dispatching `change` on the
      dropdown destroys all previously spawned entities (old references no
      longer live) and player bullets, then spawns the selected enemy type with
      its configured `count`/formation — asserted for at least two different
      keys in a boot test.
- [ ] **Panel resync**: after a selection change every slider/colour/select
      reflects the new enemy's persisted config, and a subsequent slider edit
      applies to the newly selected enemy (`currentConfig.key` updated).
- [ ] **Index layout**: `GymIndex`'s ENEMIES column contains exactly the single
      fodder row (booting `GymFodderEnemies`) plus the dedicated `GymBoss`
      row; no per-enemy rows, no Bosses column/header, no "Boss Swarm" row;
      updated `GymIndex` tests assert the new columns/labels and keyboard focus
      order.
- [ ] **Regression coverage**: existing `GymEnemies` test coverage (per-seed
      formations, panel controls, respawn, power-ups, parity) is migrated to
      `GymFodderEnemies` and passes.
- [ ] **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes
      (`npm test`), including gym-parity/equivalence guards.
- [ ] **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes — at
      minimum `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (§1.1 single reusable
      gym scene, §8.5 gym surface/editor panel, index-layout description) and
      any other docs referencing `GymEnemies` or the index columns — plus code
      comments.

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity** (`AGENTS.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`
  §5.1): an enabled gameplay object must run the same code in a gym and in the
  game; the dropdown only changes *which* config is active, never gameplay
  behaviour. Reuse `respawnFormation()` / `registerDynamicEntity()` rather than
  re-implementing destroy/spawn.
- **Discovery-driven, no hard-coded lists**: the dropdown options come from the
  config store, exactly as `discoverEnemyGymEntries()` does today.
- **Idempotent / resilient**: missing or corrupt storage must not throw (fall
  back to seed defaults, as `loadEnemyConfig` already does).
- Keep `init({ enemyKey })` supported as an optional deep-link default (useful
  for tests and any future route) unless planning decides otherwise.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption (needs producer confirmation):** per answers 1a/2b, the
  "Boss Swarm" `boss`-config row is **removed** and only the dedicated
  `GymBoss` "Boss" row moves into the ENEMIES column, with the Bosses column
  and header deleted. The `boss` archetype is therefore no longer selectable
  from the fodder dropdown. If the intent was to *retain* the "Boss Swarm" row
  inside the ENEMIES column, only step 4 changes.
- **Rename blast radius:** the string/class `GymEnemies` is referenced in
  ~20 files (comments, test harness `bootCombatGymEnemies`, parity tests,
  fixtures). Grep-sweep and rename carefully; keep the parity/equivalence
  guards green.
- **Risks:** stale-entity crash on scene restart (cf. AH-0MTPLHLZ3006MOC4) —
  the dropdown rebuild must reuse the shared respawn/registration seam to
  avoid re-introducing it; focus-manager ordering changes when a column is
  removed.
- **Scope-creep guard:** no last-selection persistence, no favourite/pinning,
  no per-enemy dropdown grouping, no dropdown for boss archetypes — record any
  such idea as a separate linked work item, not in this change.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.ts` — rename to `GymFodderEnemies.ts`; add the
  enemy `<select>` row + selection-change handler and panel resync.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.test.ts` — rename/update; add dropdown rebuild
  tests.
- `src/scenes/GymIndex.ts` — single fodder row; remove Bosses column; relocate
  `GymBoss` row; update column constants.
- `src/scenes/GymIndex.test.ts` — update column/label/focus assertions.
- `src/utils/enemyGymDiscovery.ts` — dropdown enumeration now belongs in the
  scene; repurpose or retire (and its tests).
- `src/test/powerUpTestFixtures.ts` (+ `.test.ts`) — `bootCombatGymEnemies`
  harness references the old scene.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts`, `src/scenes/core/*` (parity/equivalence tests),
  `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts`, `src/entities/enemyFire.ts` — comment/string
  references to `GymEnemies`.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — §1.1, §8.5 and index layout.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — What happens to the GymIndex ENEMIES column?**
  Answer (operator, interactive reply): **1a** — replace the per-enemy rows with
  a single row that boots the single enemy gym scene; **and also move the bosses
  into the enemies column**; **name the single scene `GymFodderEnemies`**.
- **Q2 — What does the dropdown list, and does the Bosses column change?**
  Answer (operator, interactive reply): **2b** — all configs **except `boss`**;
  remove the redundant "Boss Swarm" config row (see Q1 for the boss row
  relocation).
- **Q3 — On dropdown change, what happens to the rest of the panel and running
  state?**
  Answer (operator, interactive reply): **3a** — reload every panel control
  from the newly selected enemy's persisted config (discarding unsaved edits),
  clear player bullets and run the shared clean `respawnFormation()` path; no
  change to wave-timeout semantics.
- Sources: interactive operator replies in the intake session. Related work
  identified via Worklog search (see the automated related-work report appended
  below / in the work item).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUQUOZBC00016LQ** – F1: AOE core infrastructure (descriptor + dispatch) (completed)
- **AH-0MUWZ5HCV0034H44** – Massive Explosions and Fireworks on Victory (completed)
- **AH-0MTCNZ7DN0049K73** – Scene-level tests: GymPowerUps via gameHarness (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: acceptance, active, add, agents, already (+345 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: active, add, agents, already, also (+328 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: active, add, already, also, always (+310 more)
