# Intake Brief — New power-ups and weapons from classic arcade games

## Problem statement

AI_Hell's power-up catalogue (8 types: Shield, Bomb, Speed Boost, Phase Shift,
Teleport, Extra Life, Magnet, Mineral Scoop) and weapon catalogue (permanent
Cannon plus Spread, Dual, Rapid and the AOE family Nova, Mortar, Arc) are
coherent and well-tuned, but they were grown organically rather than
deliberately mining the **classic arcade era** for signature, instantly
recognisable player abilities. This epic researches that era and turns the
best candidates into implementable work items, so the game grows a distinctive
"arcade homage" arsenal without ad-hoc, un-scoped power-up or weapon requests.

The sibling enemy epic (AH-0MUYAQ6YH0010G52, "New enemies from classic arcade
games") established the pattern this epic mirrors: a shared research catalogue
plus one full-lifecycle child work item per selected concept.

## Users

- **As the game designer**, I want a researched, curated catalogue of classic
  arcade power-up and weapon behaviours adapted to AI_Hell's neon-vector rules,
  so new arsenal work starts from a clear design brief rather than a one-line
  wish.
- **As an implementing agent/developer**, I want each selected power-up/weapon
  to have its own work item with a user story, testable ACs, predicted key
  files and a plan that follows the existing catalogue/level-curve conventions,
  so I can implement it without re-deriving the design.
- **As the producer**, I want the candidates that were considered but not
  selected recorded, so the arsenal can be expanded later without redoing the
  research.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want to collect new arcade-inspired weapons and power-ups
  that feel distinct from the existing nine weapons and eight power-ups, so
  runs stay varied as the roster grows.
- As a **developer**, I want every new item to plug into the existing
  catalogue, level-curve, drop-weight, icon, AOE and gym-parity seams, so
  adding it does not fork the game/gym code paths.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A research document `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md` exists and catalogues at least 5 and at most 8 selected classic-arcade power-up/weapon concepts, recording for each its source game, original behaviour, adaptation to AI_Hell's neon-vector code-drawn arena, selection rationale, and whether it is a power-up or a weapon.
- The research document includes a considered-but-not-selected section listing the remaining candidates from the research pool, each with a one-line reason for deferral, so the range can be expanded later.
- One child work item exists per selected concept, each containing a user story, measurable and testable acceptance criteria including unit tests, predicted key files, and a full-lifecycle plan (catalogue entry + level-curve variables + code + tests + gym parity + docs), and each child references this epic and the research document.
- Each selected weapon's design notes specify its `WeaponId`/`WEAPON_CATALOGUE` entry, its fire subdivision on the shared 80 BPM beat grid, whether it needs a new `AoEDescriptor`/trigger or a new shared combat-core dispatch seam, and its `weaponLevels.ts` upgrade variables.
- Each selected power-up's design notes specify its `PowerUpId`/`POWER_UP_CATALOGUE` entry, its timed/stored/permanent semantics, its `powerUpLevels.ts` upgrade variables, its code-drawn icon, and its `powerUpWeights` drop weight.
- Each selected concept's notes name the gym scene(s) that will exercise it (existing `GymWeapons`, `GymPowerUpsUtility`, `GymPowerUpsCombat`, `GymFormationScene`-derived gyms, or a new gym), to satisfy the gym-to-game parity rule.
- An automated validation test asserts the research document exists, contains 5-8 selected concepts, has the deferred section, and that every selected concept names a catalogue/registry seam and a gym scene.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Neon-vector aesthetic, code-drawn graphics only** — no external art assets
  (GDD §7.2); every new drop needs a code-drawn icon in `src/powerups/icons.ts`.
- **Gym↔game parity** — an enabled gameplay object must run the same code in a
  gym and the game; shared behaviour lives in `src/scenes/core/`. Enforced by
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` and the gym-parity docs
  assertion (AGENTS.md).
- **Weapons are cumulative and timed (10 s)** and must fire on an exact
  subdivision or whole-beat multiple of the shared 80 BPM beat grid
  (`src/utils/beat.ts`, AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B).
- **Power-ups follow the temporary/permanent split** — a field pickup adds a
  temporary level tied to the item's timed window; a hold-full reward grants a
  permanent level (`src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`, AH-0MUX802450085VZZ).
- **Every item must carry a level curve** — a new weapon needs
  `WEAPON_UPGRADE_SPECS` entries (`src/utils/weaponLevels.ts`); a new power-up
  needs `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS` entries (`src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`), using
  the one shared curve (`src/utils/curve.ts`). No power-up or weapon is exempt.
- **Data-driven catalogue + drop weights** — items are entries in
  `src/powerups/types.ts` / `src/utils/weapons.ts` plus relative weights in
  `src/core/rules.ts`; tuning is data, not code.
- **"Enemies are the bullets" design** (GDD §2.4) and **no enemy–enemy
  collisions** (GDD §2.6) constrain any power-up that changes enemy behaviour
  (e.g. a Pac-Man-style frightened state).
- **Behaviours must fit a top-down free-2D arena** — the brief must state how
  each concept is translated (or note where translation is not faithful).
- **Balance guardrail** — new items must not trivialise the run or make the
  existing catalogue redundant; coverage and drop weight are part of the design
  notes.
- **Scope is research + design + child-item creation.** This epic does not
  itself implement the items; each selected concept's implementation is its own
  child work item.

## Existing state

- **Power-up catalogue** (GDD §4.4, `src/powerups/types.ts`): Shield, Bomb,
  Speed Boost, Phase Shift, Teleport, Extra Life, Magnet, Mineral Scoop —
  `PowerUpId`, `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE` (with display name and one-line
  description), `DropId` union, `isWeaponDrop()`.
- **Weapon catalogue** (`src/utils/weapons.ts`): `WeaponId`, `WEAPON_CATALOGUE`
  (offsets, side offsets, beat-subdivision fire rate, bullet colour/shape/size,
  lifetime, optional `AoEDescriptor`), `DEFAULT_WEAPON_SUBDIVISIONS`,
  `BULLET_COLORS`, `AOE_RADII`, `AOE_PROJECTILE_SPEEDS`, `AOE_WEAPON_IDS`.
- **Level curves**: `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` (`WeaponUpgradeVariable`,
  `WEAPON_UPGRADE_SPECS`, `resolveWeaponAtLevel`, on-grid quantisation) and
  `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` (`POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS`,
  `PowerUpLevelStore`), both on the single `src/utils/curve.ts` curve.
- **Effects + icons + HUD**: `src/powerups/effects.ts` (`EffectsRegistry`),
  `src/powerups/icons.ts` (`ICON_COLORS`, `WEAPON_ICON_COLORS`,
  code-drawn icons), `src/ui/HUD.ts` (merged level rows).
- **Drop pipeline**: `src/powerups/spawner.ts`
  (`WeightedRandomSpawner`/`RoundRobinSpawner`), `src/powerups/placement.ts`,
  `src/powerups/choice.ts` (hold-full choice pool), `src/core/rules.ts`
  (`powerUpWeights`, `weaponWeights`, `beatBpm`, `weaponSubdivisions`),
  `src/scenes/core/dropLayer.ts` (shared drop lifecycle).
- **AOE dispatch**: `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` /
  `CombatCoreScene.ts` read the `AoEDescriptor` and resolve `onFire`
  (Nova/Arc) and `onRandom` (Mortar) effects once for game and gyms.
- **Gym surface**: `GymWeapons` (weapon drops + help overlay),
  `GymPowerUpsUtility` (threat-free non-combat drops), `GymPowerUpsCombat`
  (combat-coupled drops), `GymFormationScene`-derived full-pool gyms,
  `GymWeaponLeveling`, `GymIndex`, `HelpScene`.
- **Precedent**: the sibling epic's `docs/CLASSIC_ENEMY_RESEARCH.md` and its
  validation guard `src/classicEnemyResearchDocs.test.ts` are the model for the
  research catalogue and its automated check.
- GDD §8 "Future Scope" already anticipates roster expansion; §4.4 documents
  9+ distinct power-up types and the AOE weapon family.

## Desired change

Produce researched, ready-to-implement power-up and weapon concepts drawn from
classic arcade games and capture each as a scoped full-lifecycle child work
item, with a shared research document acting as the catalogue and the record of
deferred candidates.

**Proposed candidate pool** (research selects 5–8; the rest go in the
"considered but not selected" section). Each candidate is anchored to the
classic-arcade source game named. The pool intentionally mixes weapons and
power-ups.

Weapons:

- Galaga — "Dual Fighter" escort/companion ship that trails the player and
  fires alongside it.
- Gradius — "Options"/"Multiple" orbiting satellites that each fire along the
  ship's heading.
- R-Type — piercing "Wave Laser" that passes through enemies (uses the
  catalogued `piercing` upgrade variable).
- Centipede — ricocheting shot that bounces off arena edges (uses the
  catalogued `bounces` upgrade variable).
- Defender / Robotron 2084 — "Smart Bomb" screen-wide enemy-clearing pulse.
- Missile Command — cluster/MIRV missile that splits into multiple warheads
  (uses the catalogued `split` upgrade variable).
- Tempest — "Superzapper" screen pulse that damages all enemies once.
- Sinistar — stored-ammo "Sinibomb" consumable (may need a new stored-ammo
  seam).

Power-ups:

- Pac-Man — "Power Pellet" that frightens enemies (they flee and stop firing)
  for a timed window.
- Space Invaders — "Mystery UFO" bonus pickup (concentrated score/minerals).
- Defender — "Smart Bomb" power-up (clears enemy bullets and damages all
  enemies once).
- Gradius — "Force Field"/reflector that bounces enemy bullets back.
- Galaga — player-side tractor/"Repulsor" that pushes enemies and bullets away.
- Frogger — "Super Leap"/invulnerability window across a hazard lane.
- Asteroids — "Decoy"/"Clay Pigeon" that draws enemy fire for a timed window.
- Gauntlet — "Potion" burst that clears nearby threats on pickup.

*(Every candidate in the pool is recorded in the research document; only 5–8
become child work items. If fewer than 5 survive the engine-constraint review,
a smaller selection is acceptable, and the shortfall is recorded with reasons.)*

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md` — New. The catalogue of selected
  and deferred concepts (the epic's primary deliverable).
- `src/classicPowerUpWeaponResearchDocs.test.ts` — New. Automated validation
  guard, following the `src/*Docs.test.ts` convention
  (`src/classicEnemyResearchDocs.test.ts`).
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — Updated (by child items). New `WeaponId` +
  `WEAPON_CATALOGUE` entries, subdivisions, colours, lifetimes, AOE
  descriptors.
- `src/powerups/types.ts` — Updated (by child items). New `PowerUpId` +
  `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE` entries and `DropId`/`WEAPON_DROP_IDS` membership.
- `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` / `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — Updated (by
  child items). Level-curve specs for each new item.
- `src/core/rules.ts` — Updated (by child items). `powerUpWeights` /
  `weaponWeights` entries.
- `src/powerups/icons.ts` — Updated (by child items). Code-drawn icons.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` / `CombatCoreScene.ts` — Updated (by child
  items) only where a new dispatch seam is unavoidable.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUps*.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/GymIndex.ts`, `src/scenes/HelpScene.ts` — Updated (by child
  items) for parity and help.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — Updated. §4.4 power-up/weapon catalogue and
  §8 future scope reference the new research document and roster.
- `README.md` — Updated. Power-up/weapon catalogue documentation.

## Related work

- **New enemies from classic arcade games (AH-0MUYAQ6YH0010G52)** — the sibling
  epic this one mirrors; its `docs/CLASSIC_ENEMY_RESEARCH.md` and validation
  guard are the direct precedent.
- **Research catalogue and engine-constraint validation (AH-0MV01EBUR003BDNK)** —
  completed; the enemy research child whose shape this epic's research child
  follows.
- **Weapon leveling (AH-0MUPMPCB2009J54J)** — completed; every new weapon must
  supply `weaponLevels.ts` variables.
- **Power-Up Leveling (AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6)** — completed; every new power-up
  must supply `powerUpLevels.ts` variables.
- **Area of effect weapons (AH-0MUOOB3OR001V8CD)** — completed; the AOE
  descriptor seam new area weapons reuse.
- **Refactor weapon fire rates as beat subdivisions and add catalogue-wide
  invariant (AH-0MUGQBN5T009U4YG)** — completed; all weapon fire rates must be
  on the 80 BPM grid.
- **Weapon power-ups (3 patterns + reset) with auto-fire and weapon gym scene
  (AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR)** — completed; the round-robin weapon gym new weapons
  extend.
- **Field power-up/weapon pickups must upgrade the item TEMPORARILY, not
  permanently (AH-0MUX802450085VZZ)** — completed; the temporary/permanent
  level split every new item follows.
- **Create gym scene for power-ups with spawning, collection, and standalone
  HUD (AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT)** — completed; the threat-free power-up gym.
- **Integrate power-up level-up offers into the hold-full choice
  (AH-0MUV5CLVO002ZHS9)** — completed; new power-ups join the hold-full choice
  pool.
- **Smart capture bot: survival-first heuristic (AH-0MUX2NENC008AHOQ)** —
  completed; automated playtests must survive any new weapon/power-up, so its
  behaviours are a useful validation input.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUD9ZNN30065ZLP** – Test: Game-over leaderboard UX (completed)
- **AH-0MUX2NENC008AHOQ** – Smart capture bot: survival-first heuristic that seeks power-ups and minerals and dodges fire patterns (completed)
- **AH-0MUKCLXLW0032R67** – enemies should accept min/max range for their starting positions on both the x and y axis. (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: arcade, capture, catalogue, child, classic (+25 more)
- `README.md` — matched: capture, catalogue, child, classic, created (+23 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0muyaq6yh0010g52, arcade, capture, catalogue, child (+22 more)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk**: the research could expand indefinitely. Mitigation —
  cap selection at 5–8 this round; record all other candidates in the deferred
  section. Extra opportunities become linked work items, not scope.
- **Balance risk**: a screen-clearing power-up (Smart Bomb / Superzapper) or a
  piercing/ricochet weapon could trivialise runs or eclipse Nova/Mortar/Arc.
  Mitigation — every item's design notes must state its rarity weight, coverage
  and how it stays distinct from the existing catalogue.
- **Pipeline-fit risk**: some concepts (companion ship, orbiting options,
  stored-ammo bombs, frightened-enemy state) cannot be expressed by the current
  catalogue alone and need new entity/dispatch seams. Mitigation — the research
  document must state, per concept, whether it maps to an existing seam (an
  `offsets`/`sideOffsets` pattern, an `AoEDescriptor`, the effects registry) or
  needs a new seam, before implementation starts.
- **Behaviour-change risk**: a Pac-Man-style frightened state changes shared
  enemy behaviour and must stay gym↔game identical (shared core, not per-scene).
- **Assumption**: "classic arcade era" means the coin-op era of the late 1970s
  to mid-1980s, anchored by the same games the enemy epic used (Space Invaders,
  Galaga, Pac-Man, Centipede, Robotron 2084, Defender, Missile Command, Frogger)
  plus the wider classic pool.
- **Assumption**: the operator-supplied candidate examples are illustrative,
  not a required final selection.
- **Assumption**: this epic's children implement the items; no separate
  implementation epic is needed.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 "How many new power-ups/weapons should this epic select and turn into
  child work items?" — Answer (operator): **(A) ~5–8 total**, mirroring the
  enemy epic, *"but if you cannot create 5+ meaningful ideas, fewer is
  acceptable"*. Source: interactive reply. Research: reviewed the existing
  8-power-up / 7-weapon catalogue and `docs/CLASSIC_ENEMY_RESEARCH.md`; a 5–8
  cap keeps each child a tractable vertical slice.
- Q2 "What should the epic itself produce?" — Answer (operator): **(A) a
  dedicated, epic-scoped research document plus one child work item per
  selection**. Source: interactive reply. Research: mirrors
  `docs/CLASSIC_ENEMY_RESEARCH.md` and the operator's enemy-epic instruction to
  record deferred candidates.
- Q3 "What should each per-item child work item deliver?" — Answer (operator):
  **(A) full lifecycle** — catalogue/config entry + level-curve variables +
  code + tests + gym parity + docs, one child per item. Source: interactive
  reply. Research: matches the enemy epic's full-lifecycle child decision.

# Research catalogue and engine-constraint validation

Part of epic **New power-ups and weapons from classic arcade games** (AH-0MV14SO0G0095IJ4).
This is the test/verification-first, primary research deliverable of the epic.

## User story

As the game designer, I want a single researched catalogue of the selected classic-arcade power-up and weapon concepts (source, adaptation, pipeline fit, level-curve inputs and gym scene) plus the deferred candidates, so the arsenal direction is traceable and future expansion does not repeat the research.

## Required content

`docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md` records, for each of the **8 selected** concepts:

Weapons (4): R-Type piercing wave laser; Centipede ricochet shot; Missile Command cluster/MIRV missile; Gradius Options orbiting satellites.

Power-ups (4): Pac-Man Power Pellet (frightened enemies); Defender Smart Bomb (clears enemy bullets and damages all enemies once); Gradius Force Field/reflector; Space Invaders Mystery UFO bonus pickup.

For each selected concept the document records: source game and era; original behaviour; AI_Hell adaptation to the top-down free-2D neon-vector code-drawn arena (including any documented divergence); whether it is a power-up or a weapon; pipeline fit; the gym scene(s) for parity; and the selection rationale.

For a **weapon** the pipeline fit specifies its `WeaponId`/`WEAPON_CATALOGUE` entry, its fire subdivision on the shared 80 BPM beat grid, whether it needs a new `AoEDescriptor`/trigger or a new shared combat-core dispatch seam (or is a catalogue entry only), and its `weaponLevels.ts` upgrade variables.

For a **power-up** the pipeline fit specifies its `PowerUpId`/`POWER_UP_CATALOGUE` entry, its timed/stored/permanent semantics, its `powerUpLevels.ts` upgrade variables, its code-drawn icon, and its `powerUpWeights` drop weight.

A **"Considered but not selected"** section lists the remaining research-pool candidates (Galaga Dual Fighter, Defender/Robotron Smart Bomb weapon form, Tempest Superzapper, Sinistar Sinibomb, Galaga Repulsor, Frogger Super Leap, Asteroids Decoy, Gauntlet Potion) with a one-line deferral reason each.

## Verification

A Vitest docs guard (`src/classicPowerUpWeaponResearchDocs.test.ts`, matching the `src/*Docs.test.ts` convention) asserts the research document exists, contains 5-8 selected concepts, has the deferred section, and that every selected concept names a catalogue/registry seam and a gym scene. TDD: write the guard first, then make it pass.

## Key Files

- `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md` - New. The catalogue of selected and deferred concepts.
- `src/classicPowerUpWeaponResearchDocs.test.ts` - New. Automated validation guard.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` - Updated. Section 4.4 references the research document.

## Implementation plan

1. Write the failing docs guard first (TDD), asserting existence, count, deferred section, seams and gym scenes.
2. Draft `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md` with the 8 selected concepts and the deferred section.
3. Cross-link the document from `docs/Game Design Document.md` section 4.4.
4. Run the guard and the full suite until green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The research document `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md` exists and catalogues at least 5 and at most 8 selected classic-arcade power-up/weapon concepts, recording for each its source game, original behaviour, adaptation to AI_Hell's neon-vector code-drawn arena, selection rationale, and whether it is a power-up or a weapon.
- The research document includes a considered-but-not-selected section listing the remaining candidates from the research pool, each with a one-line reason for deferral, so the range can be expanded later.
- Each selected weapon's design notes specify its `WeaponId`/`WEAPON_CATALOGUE` entry, its fire subdivision on the shared 80 BPM beat grid, whether it needs a new `AoEDescriptor`/trigger or a new shared combat-core dispatch seam, and its `weaponLevels.ts` upgrade variables.
- Each selected power-up's design notes specify its `PowerUpId`/`POWER_UP_CATALOGUE` entry, its timed/stored/permanent semantics, its `powerUpLevels.ts` upgrade variables, its code-drawn icon, and its `powerUpWeights` drop weight.
- Each selected concept's notes name the gym scene(s) that will exercise it (existing `GymWeapons`, `GymPowerUpsUtility`, `GymPowerUpsCombat`, `GymFormationScene`-derived gyms, or a new gym), to satisfy the gym-to-game parity rule.
- An automated validation test asserts the research document exists, contains 5-8 selected concepts, has the deferred section, and that every selected concept names a catalogue/registry seam and a gym scene.
- Full project test suite passes with the new document and validation test.

# R-Type piercing wave laser

Part of epic **New power-ups and weapons from classic arcade games** (AH-0MV14SO0G0095IJ4).
Design brief: `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md` (selected concept: **R-Type**).
Implements one selected classic-arcade weapon as a full vertical slice (catalogue entry, level-curve variables, code, tests, gym parity, code comments).

## User story

As a player, I want a piercing wave laser that passes through ordinary enemies, so that lining up a column of foes rewards positioning and feels like the classic R-Type beam.

## Source and adaptation

- **Source:** R-Type (Irem, 1987)
- **Original behaviour:** the Wave Laser is a charged beam that travels the screen, damaging multiple enemies in its path rather than stopping at the first target.
- **AI_Hell adaptation:** a timed weapon that fires a beam bullet which, on hitting an enemy, damages it and continues to travel (passing through) up to its pierce budget. Unlike the ship's conventional single-hit bullets the beam survives the first hit. Neon-vector code-drawn elongated bolt; no enemy-enemy interaction.

## Pipeline fit

- **Catalogue:** new `WeaponId` `'wave_laser'` plus a `WEAPON_CATALOGUE` entry (offsets, fire rate, bullet colour/shape/size, lifetime).
- **Beat grid:** fire rate set as an exact subdivision of the 80 BPM beat grid via `weaponSubdivisions` (a whole-beat multiple is acceptable for a heavy beam); the `isOnBeatGrid` invariant must hold.
- **Dispatch seam:** no new `AoEDescriptor`; requires the shared combat-core bullet/enemy collision path to honour a **pierce budget**. If no base piercing is expressible today, add a neutral `piercing` field to `WeaponDefinition`, read once by the shared core so game and gyms share the seam.
- **Level curve:** consumes the `weaponLevels.ts` variable `piercing` (base 0; the weapon supplies its base pierce count, growing toward the spec cap).

## Gym parity

`GymWeapons` (existing) — the weapon joins the weapon drop round-robin and the help overlay. The pierce behaviour lives in the shared combat core (`src/scenes/core/`), so game and gym are identical; `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` must stay green.

## Key Files

- `src/utils/weapons.ts` - Updated. New `WeaponId`, `WEAPON_CATALOGUE` entry, subdivision, colour, lifetime.
- `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` - Updated. Base `piercing` value consumed by the resolver.
- `src/core/rules.ts` - Updated. `weaponWeights` and `weaponSubdivisions` entries.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` / `CombatScene.ts` - Updated. Shared pierce-budget bullet behaviour.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` - Exercised for parity (no change expected).
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` - Exercised; the weapon appears in the merged timed-weapon rows.

## Implementation plan

1. Add failing tests for the catalogue entry and pierce-budget bullet behaviour.
2. Add `'wave_laser'` to `WeaponId`, `WEAPON_CATALOGUE`, `weaponSubdivisions`, `weaponWeights` and the drop round-robin.
3. Implement the shared pierce-budget behaviour once in `src/scenes/core/`.
4. Wire the weapon into the timed weapon set, HUD and help overlay.
5. Run `GymWeapons` for parity and run the full suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- This work item is the per-selected-concept child for R-Type: it contains a user story, measurable/testable acceptance criteria including unit tests, predicted key files, and a full-lifecycle plan (catalogue entry + level-curve variables + code + tests + gym parity + docs), and references the epic AH-0MV14SO0G0095IJ4 and `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md`.
- The weapon's design notes specify its `WeaponId`/`WEAPON_CATALOGUE` entry, its fire subdivision on the shared 80 BPM beat grid, whether it needs a new `AoEDescriptor`/trigger or a new shared combat-core dispatch seam, and its `weaponLevels.ts` upgrade variables.
- The design notes name the gym scene that exercises the weapon (`GymWeapons`), and the implemented behaviour runs the same shared code in the gym and the game (enforced by `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`).
- A fired wave-laser bullet damages and passes through up to its pierce budget of enemies and stops once the budget is exhausted; the pierce budget boundary is unit-tested.
- The weapon's fire rate satisfies `isOnBeatGrid` for its configured subdivision, verified by a unit test.
- The weapon's `piercing` upgrade variable resolves through `resolveWeaponAtLevel` and increases the pierce budget monotonically within the spec cap, verified by a unit test.
- The weapon is reachable as a timed weapon drop and its HUD/help row renders from the catalogue, verified by a test.
- Full project test suite passes with the new weapon and all new tests.

As a player, I want orbiting satellite pods that trail my ship and fire alongside me, so that building the escort changes my fire pattern and feels like the classic Gradius Options.

Part of epic **New power-ups and weapons from classic arcade games** (AH-0MV14SO0G0095IJ4).

## User story

As a player, I want a power pellet that frightens nearby enemies so they flee and stop firing for a timed window, so that collecting it flips the pressure of a wave and feels like the classic Pac-Man reversal. This is the highest-risk concept: it changes shared enemy behaviour and must be gym-to-game identical.

## Source and adaptation

- **Source:** Pac-Man (Namco, 1980)
- **Original behaviour:** eating a power pellet frightens the ghosts, who turn blue, flee the player and become edible for a limited time.
- **AI_Hell adaptation:** a timed power-up that puts affected enemies into a **frightened** state for a window: they flee the ship and stop firing; colliding with a frightened enemy destroys it. No enemy-enemy collisions are introduced (GDD section 2.6), and "enemies are the bullets" (GDD section 2.4) is preserved because firing is simply suppressed while frightened.

## Pipeline fit

- **Catalogue:** new `PowerUpId` `'power_pellet'` plus a `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE` entry.
- **Semantics:** timed field pickup; the fright window is the item's timed window.
- **Level curve:** consumes `powerUpLevels.ts` variables (fright duration, radius/count), resolved through `resolvePowerUpAtLevel` on the shared curve.
- **Behaviour seam:** needs a **new shared enemy-behaviour state** in `src/scenes/core/` (a pure "frightened" decision consumed by enemy steering and fire dispatch), never per-scene, so game and gyms cannot diverge.
- **Icon / weight:** code-drawn icon in `src/powerups/icons.ts`; relative weight in `powerUpWeights` (`src/core/rules.ts`).

## Gym parity

`GymPowerUpsCombat` (existing) exercises combat-coupled drops; `GymEnemies`/`GymFormationScene`-derived gyms exercise the shared frightened steering. The state lives in the shared core, so game and gym are identical; `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` must stay green.

- `src/ui/HUD.ts` - Exercised; the power-up row renders from the catalogue.

2. Add `'power_pellet'` to `PowerUpId`, `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE`, `DropId`, `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS`, icons and `powerUpWeights`.
3. Implement the shared frightened state once in `src/scenes/core/`; consume it from enemy steering and fire dispatch.

5. Run the combat power-up gym and the formation gym for parity; run the full suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- This work item is the per-selected-concept child for Pac-Man: it contains a user story, measurable/testable acceptance criteria including unit tests, predicted key files, and a full-lifecycle plan (catalogue entry + level-curve variables + code + tests + gym parity + docs), and references the epic AH-0MV14SO0G0095IJ4 and `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md`.

- Colliding with a frightened enemy destroys it and does not destroy the ship, verified by a test; no enemy-enemy collision behaviour is introduced.

**Test-first note:** the implement finish gate requires a green suite, so red tests cannot be committed alone. If the red window cannot be committed, land this child together with **C2 CLI surface** as one coherent green change (precedent: F1 `AH-0MUX9T6L9004KCDV` under parent `AH-0MUX802450085VZZ`).

With no `--output`, default names append the iteration index to the existing timestamped name so tight loops cannot collide.

## User story

As a maintainer, I want `npm run capture -- --count 3` to produce three predictably named files, so I can collect a batch without a shell loop.

## Key Files

- `scripts/capture-gameplay.test.ts` — make the C1 contract tests pass
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — record the naming rules

## Acceptance Criteria

- `npm run capture -- --count 3` produces 3 distinct non-trivial `.webm` files in `capture-output/` and exits 0.
- `-n` is accepted as a short alias for `--count`.
- Omitting `--count` behaves exactly as today (single clip, no regression).

- `--output` + `--count > 1` behaviour is deterministic, documented and covered by a test.
- Unit tests cover arg parsing (default, valid, invalid, alias) and the multi-output path resolver.

# Bot to use the reverse thrusters — Intake Brief

**Priority:** critical · **Issue type:** feature · **Assignees:** Map

## Problem statement

The shipped demo/attract bot (and the competent steering layer it drives) never
uses the reverse thruster: `toAsteroidsInput()` in `src/ai/botHumanLike.ts`
hard-emits `reverse: false`, and the steering/forward model has no concept of
retro-thrust. As a result the bot can only slow down by coasting on friction and
must spin ~180° to travel backwards — it is visibly less capable than a human
using the same controls. We want the bot to treat reverse as a first-class thrust
option (brake-assist, heading-aware thrust, and aim-preserving retreat) while
respecting the ship's reverse configuration and remaining human-like.

## Users

- **Player watching the attract/demo** (primary): expects a believable pilot that
  uses the same control scheme and thruster set as the player, so the demo is a
  meaningful preview of the game.
- **Developer / designer** (secondary): needs the bot to honour a player's ship
  configuration, including a player who disabled the reverse thruster.

Example user stories:

- As a player watching the demo, the bot brakes with retro-thrust instead of
  overshooting a mineral, so the demo looks skilled.
- As a player watching the bot retreat from a threat with its nose still on the
  enemy (kiting), the ship flies like a competent human rather than an impostor.
- As a player who switched the reverse thruster off, the demo bot never uses it
  either, so the demo matches my handling.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — Reverse as brake-assist.** When the bot's nose is (near) aligned with
   its desired travel bearing and its predicted stopping distance exceeds the
   remaining gap, it may hold reverse thrust to decelerate rather than only
   coasting on friction. Braking with reverse must not increase overshoot versus
   the current friction-only model in the covered scenarios.
2. **AC2 — Heading-aware thrust direction.** When the desired travel bearing is
   behind the ship (heading error beyond a configured threshold), the bot thrusts
   **in reverse** toward it instead of always turning 180° to face it. The
   forward/reverse choice is stable across ticks (no oscillation around the
   threshold).
3. **AC3 — Aim-preserving retreat (kiting).** While engaging or avoiding a hazard
   and needing to increase separation, the bot may hold reverse to retreat while
   keeping its nose on its aim target — avoiding the current turn-away behaviour.
4. **AC4 — Config-respecting enable flag.** Reverse metres are only emitted when
   the ship's reverse thruster is enabled (`ShipConfig.asteroidsReverseEnabled`);
   when it is disabled, the bot emits `reverse: false` on every input and behaves
   exactly as today. Numeric customisation of the bot's *model* to live thruster
   values is tracked separately (see Related work / AH-0MV268RXJ007M7A9).
5. **AC5 — Human-like reverse cadence.** Reverse input is held in human-like
   presses (min/max duration with per-press jitter) using the same press-cadence
   mechanism as forward thrust; the bot never toggles reverse every frame, and
   the W/A/D restriction is otherwise preserved.
6. **AC6 — Contract & guard updated.** `toAsteroidsInput()` and the governor
   emit `reverse: true` only when the committed intent requests it, and the
   explicit `reverse: false` structural guarantee (plus its test) from
   AH-0MV13LZ08008DN3E is replaced by the new contract.
7. **AC7 — Testing / validation.** Unit tests cover reverse selection for
   brake-assist, heading-aware thrust, kiting, and the disabled-config path, plus
   the reverse press cadence. A deterministic integration test demonstrates the
   bot reversing in a target-behind scenario and reaching it with fewer/no 180°
   turns. Existing bot determinism (seeded RNG, dt-driven) is preserved.
8. **AC8 — Documentation.** `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` (and any reverse-thruster
   docs) describe the bot's reverse behaviour, the enable-flag gating, and the
   human-like reverse press model.
9. **AC9 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity:** the changed behaviour must live in the shared core
  (`src/ai/**`) and be consumed by both `PlayScene` and any gym/eval harness that
  drives the bot; no divergent copy.
- **Determinism:** all decisions remain a function of the injected `dt` and
  seeded RNG, so bot behaviour stays reproducible and unit-testable.
- **Physics limits:** reverse acceleration and the reverse speed cap are
  independent of forward values, and reverse must never abruptly brake
  pre-existing faster momentum (per `AsteroidsModel`).
- **Scope:** the bot's *internal model* consuming live numeric thruster config is
  a follow-up (AH-0MV268RXJ007M7A9); this item only needs the reverse-enable flag
  plus the reverse decision logic.

## Existing state

- `src/ai/botHumanLike.ts` — `toAsteroidsInput()` resolves an Asteroids input
  from a steering intent and **always** sets `reverse: false` (including the idle
  input); this is the single hard block. The governor holds forward-thrust presses
  for a jittered duration drawn from `BotHumanInputTunables`.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts` — `mayThrust()` decides forward thrust
  from `frictionDeceleration`; `planSteering()`/`buildIntent()` produce a
  direction + thrust flag with no reverse representation.
- `src/ai/botDecision.ts` — `BotSteeringIntent` = four-directional booleans +
  `dirX`/`dirY` + `thrust` + `longTravel`; no reverse field.
- `src/utils/movementModel.ts` — `AsteroidsModel.tick()` already applies reverse
  physics (`reverseEnabled`, `reverseAcceleration`, `reverseMaxSpeed`) and the
  nose-engine VFX.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `botGovernor.update(decide(...), dt, { scheme,
  facing })`; the brain is built with no config, so ShipConfig is not currently
  available to the bot.
- `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` documents the no-reverse guarantee and must change.

## Desired change

Introduce a first-class forward/reverse thrust direction in the bot's steering
intent and act on it:

1. Add a reverse-aware thrust decision to the competent steering layer
   (brake-assist + heading-aware direction + kiting), with tunables for the
   heading threshold and reverse press timing.
2. Extend `BotSteeringIntent` (and the governor's `SteeredIntent`) with a reverse
   flag, and have `toAsteroidsInput()` emit `reverse: true` accordingly.
3. Gate reverse on the ship's enable flag (wired from `PlayScene` / snapshot
   context).
4. Hold reverse in human-like presses, mirroring the forward press cadence.
5. Update the guard test/docs to the new contract; add coverage for all paths.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ai/botHumanLike.ts` — add reverse press cadence; emit `reverse` from the intent; replace the always-false guarantee and update module docs.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts` — add tunables: heading-error threshold for reverse, reverse press min/max ms, enable-flag default.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts` — heading-aware forward/reverse selection and a reverse-aware thrust predicate alongside `mayThrust()`.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/behaviours.ts` — engage/reposition behaviours choose reverse for kiting and target-behind approaches.
- `src/ai/botDecision.ts` — extend `BotSteeringIntent` with a reverse flag; keep the four-directional projection valid.
- `src/ai/botSnapshot.ts` / `src/ai/framework/worldModel.ts` — surface the reverse-enable flag (and, for the follow-up, full thruster config) to the decision layer.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — pass the ship's reverse-enable flag into the governor/brain context.
- Tests: `src/ai/botHumanLike.test.ts`, `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.test.ts`, `.../behaviours.test.ts`, `.../competentBot.integration.test.ts`, `src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts`.
- `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` — document the new reverse behaviour.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the reverse-enable flag can be surfaced to the bot cheaply
  (snapshot/context) without the full config feed tracked in AH-0MV268RXJ007M7A9.
- **Risk (behaviour regression):** adding a reverse branch can destabilise the
  existing turn/thrust decisions near the heading threshold — mitigate with a
  hysteresis/dead-band and deterministic unit tests.
- **Risk (parity):** leaving reverse logic in the demo-only layer would diverge
  from gyms — mitigate by placing the decision in the shared `src/ai/**` core.
- **Risk (physics mismatch):** the bot must not assume reverse can out-brake the
  forward speed cap; reverse is capped at `reverseMaxSpeed` and never abruptly
  brakes pre-existing momentum.
- **Risk (scope creep):** full live-config model integration is deliberately
  deferred to AH-0MV268RXJ007M7A9 (medium); any further thruster work discovered
  during implementation should become a linked work item, not in-scope here.
- **Assumption:** the demo bot continues to drive whichever control scheme the
  ship is configured with; this item only extends the `asteroids` scheme actuator.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUZCSB4B00107RG** — Add a reverse thruster to the Asteroids ship control
  scheme (parent capability; reverse physics + config).
- **AH-0MV13LZ08008DN3E** — Guard the demo bot and resolve the dead `layerDrop`
  action: deliberately asserted `reverse: false`; this item supersedes that
  guarantee and must update its test.
- **AH-0MV268RXJ007M7A9** — Bot steering model to consume live `ShipConfig`
  thruster values (medium, discovered-from this item; the auto-adjust follow-up).
- **AH-0MUXYOV4C008MV0L** — Demo bot movement goals (overshoot / look-ahead).
- **AH-0MUYRJQE50021T4A** — Bot is more gentle on the thrusters.
- **AH-0MV1DUSM2005HL98** — Bot rotation skills (related thruster-willingness).
- Docs: `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §5.1
  (parity convention), GDD §2.2.

## Follow-up created

**AH-0MV268RXJ007M7A9 — Bot steering model to consume live `ShipConfig` thruster
values** (medium, task). Evaluation result: the bot does **not** automatically
adjust to thruster-configuration changes — its forward model is hard-coded
(`frictionDeceleration: 100`, `playerSpeed: 175`) and `PlayScene` never passes
`ShipConfig` to `createCompetentBotBrain()`. The follow-up feeds the live config
into the bot's model.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1: How should the bot use reverse thrust?** — Answer (operator, interactive):
  **"All"** — brake-assist (A), heading-aware thrust (B), and aim-preserving
  kiting (C). Captured as AC1/AC2/AC3. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2: Should reverse respect the ship config and human-like cadence?** — Answer
  (operator, interactive): **"A and B"** — respect `asteroidsReverseEnabled` and
  gate reverse behind a human-like press cadence (A) while reusing the existing
  thrust-press timing mechanism (B). Captured as AC4/AC5. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3: Scope of the medium-priority auto-adjust follow-up?** — Answer (operator,
  interactive): **"A"** — feed the live `ShipConfig` (forward thrust, max speed,
  friction, and reverse accel/max speed/enabled) into the bot's model + steering.
  Created as **AH-0MV268RXJ007M7A9** (medium, task, discovered-from this item).
  Source: interactive reply.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUDZFBYY008P7ZE** – Gym scenes index not navigable by keyboard (completed)
- **AH-0MUX4975J0045VDZ** – Documentation for attract/demo mode and bot (completed)
- **AH-0MUUM3KYX008ABSW** – Test migration + verify: Update existing tests and verify parity (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0muyrjqe50021t4a, 0muzcsb4b00107rg, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+357 more)
- `README.md` — matched: 0muyrjqe50021t4a, ac1, ac3, ac4, ac5 (+331 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: ac1, ac3, ac4, ac5, act (+272 more)
---

## Plan: feature decomposition

Decomposed into 7 vertical slices (test-first ordering). No new clarifying
questions were required: the intake Appendix (Q1-Q3) already fixes
brake-assist + heading-aware thrust + kiting, enable-flag gating, and the
human-like press cadence. Planning assumptions are recorded below.

| # | Slice | Covers parent AC | Depends on |
|---|-------|------------------|------------|
| 1 | Reverse behaviour test harness and baseline (AH-0MV2JT0TF008T3OW) | AC7 | — |
| 2 | Reverse intent and enable-flag plumbing (AH-0MV2JT18K006YU35) | AC4, AC6 | 1 |
| 3 | Brake-assist reverse thrust (AH-0MV2JT1P7006KXFK) | AC1 | 2 |
| 4 | Heading-aware thrust direction (AH-0MV2JT2560098ETZ) | AC2 | 2 |
| 5 | Aim-preserving retreat (kiting) (AH-0MV2JT2LE002SIEP) | AC3 | 2, 4 |
| 6 | Human-like reverse press cadence (AH-0MV2JT30L000HT53) | AC5 | 2 |
| 7 | Documentation and full-suite verification (AH-0MV2JT3GM001BDKG) | AC8, AC9 | 3, 4, 5, 6 |

### Planning assumptions

- The heading-error threshold and the forward/reverse hysteresis band are
  tunables added in slice 4, so the exact numeric value is an
  implementation-tuning decision, not a plan blocker.
- Kiting (slice 5) reuses the existing `engage`/`evade` paths with a new
  reverse-retreat branch; no new goal band is introduced.
- The AC coverage helper's automated extractor reads only `- ` bullets, and
  this description uses a numbered AC list, so parent-AC coverage was verified
  manually against the mapping table above (all nine parent ACs map to a
  slice).

### Appendix: clarifying questions & answers (plan session)

- No new questions were asked in this planning session. The intake Appendix
  entries (Q1 "All" reverse uses; Q2 "A and B" config + cadence; Q3 "A" live
  config follow-up) remain authoritative and were used as the plan input.

# Enemy classification system for balanced wave design

**Priority:** high · **Issue type:** feature

## Problem statement

Wave designers need a data-driven **enemy classification** focused on **movement
and attack styles** so that wave composition can be designed and verified for
balance. Today `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` describes each archetype with
low-level tuning fields (`formationKind`, `shotPattern`, speeds, `health`), but
there is no field that states an archetype's *behavioural role* — whether it
holds formation and does not directly attack, roams independently, chases the
player, or shoots at them. This item adds two high-level classification columns
to the enemy CSV and wires them through the codec, gym editor and documentation.

## Users

- **Wave designer / producer** — composes waves from classified archetypes and
  wants to reason about a wave's mix of movement/attack roles at a glance.
- **Sequencer / difficulty tooling** (future, AH-0MV29XQ0H009P9WP) — will
  consume the classification to enforce balance rules (e.g. opening waves
  formation-only; cap chaser counts).
- **Developer / AI agent** — needs a documented, validated enum with a codec and
  tests, consistent with the existing data-driven enemy pipeline.

Example user stories:

- As a wave designer, I want to filter archetypes by `movementClass` so that a
  wave's movement mix is obvious without reading every low-level field.
- As a balance reviewer, I want to see at a glance that no wave is all
  `chaser`/`projectile` and that opening waves are `formation`/`contact`.
- As a developer, I want a new archetype to fail validation if it declares an
  unknown classification, so the CSV stays consistent.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — Classification vocabulary.** Two orthogonal fields are defined:
   - `movementClass`: `formation | diver | chaser | patroller | roamer`
   - `attackClass`: `contact | projectile | beam | area`

   A documented invariant states that **every** enemy damages the player on
   contact, so `attackClass` describes the archetype's ranged/special attack
   (`contact` = contact-only). The vocabulary is broader than the existing
   `formationKind`/`shotPattern` axes (it groups several of their values).
2. **AC2 — CSV data populated.** Both columns are added to
   `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` for all 18 archetype rows with the values in
   § Mapping. Absent values are coerced to documented defaults:
   `movementClass` → `formation`; `attackClass` → derived from `shotPattern`
   (`none` → `contact`, otherwise `projectile`).
3. **AC3 — Codec / type wiring.** `EnemyConfig` gains typed `movementClass` and
   `attackClass` fields (`src/core/configTypes.ts`); seed defaults updated
   (`src/core/configDefaults.ts`); `ENEMY_COLUMN_ORDER` extended;
   `validateEnemyConfig()` rejects unknown values; `coerceEnemyConfig()` applies
   the documented fallback; `serializeEnemyConfigs()` round-trips. Unit tests
   cover every path.
4. **AC4 — Gym editor.** `src/scenes/gym/GymFodderEnemies.ts` exposes both
   fields as select dropdowns (`data-config` selectors), persisted through the
   existing CSV save path; gym↔game parity is preserved (data-only change).
5. **AC5 — Documentation.** `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` is
   updated: §1 roster table gains both columns; §8 schema table lists the new
   fields with descriptions and defaults; the CSV header comment block documents
   the columns.
6. **AC6 — Testing / validation.** Unit tests cover enum validation, coercion +
   absent-value defaults, seed-CSV completeness (every row carries a valid
   pair), gym-editor selects and persistence, and serialize round-trip. **Full
   project test suite must pass with the new changes.**
7. **AC7 — Documentation completeness.** All related documentation is updated to
   reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki
   or docs site entries.

## Mapping (agreed with producer)

| key | movementClass | attackClass |
|---|---|---|
| scout | formation | projectile |
| diver | diver | projectile |
| tank | formation | projectile |
| phaser | formation | projectile |
| swarm | formation | projectile |
| boss | formation | projectile |
| march | formation | projectile |
| capturer | formation | beam |
| ghost-chase | chaser | contact |
| ghost-ambush | chaser | contact |
| ghost-flank | chaser | contact |
| ghost-wander | chaser | contact |
| grunt | chaser | contact |
| raider | patroller | projectile |
| asteroid | roamer | contact |
| harvester | roamer | contact |
| lane-traffic | roamer | contact |
| orbital-strike | roamer | area |

**Movement classes:** `formation` (coordinated/patterned, no independent
pursuit), `diver` (formation that breaks off into a targeted dive), `chaser`
(homes on the player), `patroller` (independent path that may commit to an
attack run), `roamer` (independent trajectory/hazard, ignores the player).

**Attack classes:** `contact` (contact-only), `projectile` (fires projectiles),
`beam` (tractor beam), `area` (telegraphed area detonation).

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity:** classification is data-only (no gameplay code change);
  future consumption must live in the shared core and be consumed by both game
  and gyms (see AGENTS.md gym↔game parity).
- **Backward compatibility:** existing CSV rows without the new columns must
  still parse; absent values use the documented defaults, so behaviour is
  unchanged.
- **No sequencer change in scope:** this item is descriptive/validated only;
  integration into wave generation is deferred to AH-0MV29XQ0H009P9WP.
- **Storage architecture:** SQLite is the runtime source of truth; the CSV is
  committed and parsed at boot. Never edit `.worklog` JSONL manually.

## Desired change

1. Add `EnemyMovementClass` / `EnemyAttackClass` unions and `EnemyConfig` fields
   in `src/core/configTypes.ts`, with JSDoc and the contact invariant.
2. Add the two columns to `ENEMY_COLUMN_ORDER` and `VALID_MOVEMENT_CLASSES` /
   `VALID_ATTACK_CLASSES` in `src/core/csv.ts`; extend
   `validateEnemyConfig()` and `coerceEnemyConfig()` (with documented defaults),
   and confirm `serializeEnemyConfigs()` emits the columns.
3. Populate `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` header comments and all 18 rows.
4. Update `src/core/configDefaults.ts` seed values for every archetype.
5. Add the two `_selectRow` controls in `GymFodderEnemies.ts`.
6. Update the docs and add tests per AC6.

## Existing state

- `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` — one row per archetype (18 rows; centipede is a
  dedicated entity, not a CSV row).
- `src/core/configTypes.ts` — `EnemyConfig` interface; `formationKind` and
  `shotPattern` typed unions.
- `src/core/csv.ts` — `ENEMY_COLUMN_ORDER`, `validateEnemyConfig()`,
  `coerceEnemyConfig()`, `serializeEnemyConfigs()`; existing enum validation
  pattern for `formationKind` / `shotPattern`.
- `src/core/configDefaults.ts` — seed fallbacks for all archetypes.
- `src/core/configStore.ts` / `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts` — CSV is the
  runtime source of truth, editable in dev, read-only in production.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymFodderEnemies.ts` — editor panel with `formationKind` /
  `shotPattern` selects (`_selectRow`), difficulty readout.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` — add the two classification columns, header
  documentation and values for all 18 rows.
- `src/core/configTypes.ts` — add the enum unions and `EnemyConfig` fields.
- `src/core/configDefaults.ts` — seed classification values per archetype.
- `src/core/csv.ts` — column order, enum validation, coercion + defaults.
- `src/core/csv.test.ts` — codec validation/coercion/round-trip tests.
- `src/data/csv-seed.test.ts` — seed completeness and validity assertions.
- `src/core/configStore.test.ts`, `src/core/enemyConfig.test.ts` — registry
  loader coverage for the new fields.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymFodderEnemies.ts` — editor selects.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymFodderEnemies.test.ts` — editor select/persistence tests.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — roster and schema documentation.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the column names `movementClass` / `attackClass` are accepted
  (producer approved the two-orthogonal-fields shape and the vocabulary).
- **Assumption:** `attackClass` absent-value derivation from `shotPattern` is
  acceptable as a backward-compat default. Note: `capturer` has
  `shotPattern: none` but `attackClass: beam`, and `orbital-strike` has
  `shotPattern: none` but `attackClass: area`; the derivation only applies when
  the column is absent, and the committed CSV always carries explicit values.
- **Risk (serialization/plugin):** extending `ENEMY_COLUMN_ORDER` can break
  round-trip tests or the dev CSV plugin's column validation — mitigate with
  explicit round-trip and plugin tests.
- **Risk (gym editor):** extra panel rows could affect layout or existing
  selectors — mitigate by reusing `_selectRow` and the existing `data-config`
  test query pattern.
- **Risk (scope creep):** sequencer/balance-rule integration is deliberately
  deferred to AH-0MV29XQ0H009P9WP; any further work discovered during
  implementation becomes a linked work item, not in-scope here.
- **Risk (stale worktrees):** other worktrees hold copies of
  `enemy-configs.csv`; they are out of scope for this item.

## Related work

- **Enemy Design tooling** (AH-0MTFP7EIC004F1MN) — the data-driven enemy
  pipeline this extends.
- **Design a mechanism for calculating how hard an enemy is to survive**
  (AH-0MTZWZ7MC002B01K) — the difficulty index; classification complements it
  for wave composition.
- **Implement runtime auto-sequencer for dynamic difficulty adjustment**
  (AH-0MUDIWETP003XC3X) — the sequencer that will consume the classification.
- **Integrate enemy classification into wave generation and balance tooling**
  (AH-0MV29XQ0H009P9WP) — the follow-up integration item (blocked by this item).
- **CSV seed data files (enemy-configs.csv, ship-config.csv)**
  (AH-0MUE2MGM0001XEH9) — the seed file this modifies.
- Docs: `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §1, §8, §9;
  `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.1; `docs/CLASSIC_ENEMY_RESEARCH.md`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1: Field shape — one combined column or two orthogonal columns?** — Answer
  (operator, interactive): **A — two orthogonal columns** (`movementClass` +
  `attackClass`), i.e. coarser behavioural groupings that sit above the existing
  `formationKind` / `shotPattern` axes. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2: Consumption scope — descriptive now or machine-consumed now?** — Answer
  (operator, interactive): **A — descriptive + validated now**; the integration
  into wave generation/balance tooling is a separate follow-up item. Created as
  **AH-0MV29XQ0H009P9WP** (medium, feature, blocked by this item). Source:
  interactive reply.
- **Q3: Proposed vocabulary — remove `none`?** — Answer (operator, interactive):
  **"There is no 'none' all enemies will damage the player if touched."**
  Captured as the contact invariant; `none` removed from the attack vocabulary.
  Source: interactive reply.
- **Q4: Attack encoding — single primary value vs multi-value contact set?** —
  Answer (operator, interactive): **Option 1 — single primary value; contact is
  universal** (`contact` = contact-only; ranged/special attacks are
  `projectile` / `beam` / `area`), with the mapping above confirmed. Source:
  interactive reply.

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUQUOZBC00016LQ** – F1: AOE core infrastructure (descriptor + dispatch) (completed)

# Intake Brief — Add 5 new levels before the boss showcasing the classic-arcade enemy roster

**Work item:** AH-0MV29SBAQ000HQR2 (feature, high)
**Headline:** Grow the campaign from 5 to 10 regular levels (plus the boss) so the
eight classic-arcade enemies added this sprint are showcased in curated, varied
encounters, with every player-targeting archetype paired alongside other kinds
of enemies.

## Problem statement

This sprint delivered eight classic-arcade enemy archetypes (Space Invaders
`march`, Galaga `capturer`, Pac-Man ghosts, Centipede, Robotron `grunt` horde,
Defender `raider`, Missile Command `orbital-strike`, Frogger `lane-traffic`),
but the shipped campaign is still only five levels: Levels 1–3 formation drift
(no fire), Level 4 enemy fire, Level 5 orbital Phasers. The new roster is only
reachable in the gym scenes — a player completing a normal run never sees it.

The operator wants **five more levels before the boss** to show the new enemies
off, and because some of the new enemies specifically target the player, those
archetypes must appear **alongside other kinds of enemies** rather than in
isolation.

## Users

- **Player** — "As a player, I want the run to keep escalating with genuinely
  new enemy movement and attack styles, so the campaign does not feel like the
  same five levels with more bullets."
- **Designer/content author** — "As a designer, I want a deterministic,
  data-driven way to place a specific new archetype in a specific wave pairing,
  while still letting some waves vary between runs."
- **Engineer** — "As an engineer, I want the campaign to grow through the
  existing `LEVELS` skeleton + difficulty-curve config, with gym↔game parity,
  so the change is testable and adds no divergent code paths."

## Existing state

- `src/waves/Formations.ts` defines `LEVELS` (5 static levels) and
  `LEVEL_COUNT = LEVELS.length`; the boss (`BOSS_ENEMY_KEY = 'boss'`) is
  triggered after the final level clears.
- `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` + `src/core/configStore.ts`
  (`defaultDifficultyCurves`) provide the per-wave generation layer
  (`curve` / `fixed` / `dynamic`); `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` merges it over
  the static skeleton and appends configured levels beyond `LEVEL_COUNT`.
- `WaveManager.levelCount` / `isFinalLevel` derive from `levels.length`, so
  HUD `Level N of 5` and the boss trigger adapt automatically once more levels
  exist (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` reads them).
- Spawner-gated archetypes are wave opt-in flags: `ghosts`, `centipede`,
  `horde`, `laneTraffic`; `march`, `capturer`, `raider`, `orbital-strike`,
  `lane-traffic` are CSV-backed rows. `defaultCandidatePool()` (the `dynamic`
  source) excludes `harvester`, `asteroid` and `grunt` (spawner-delivered).
- `HARVESTER_MIN_LEVEL = 4`, `HARVESTER_MAX_LEVEL = 5` — the Harvester only
  spawns in the two hardest regular levels and must be re-ranged for 10 levels.

## Desired change

Grow the campaign to **10 regular levels + the boss**, keeping Levels 1–3 as
the no-fire onboarding section and introducing/interleaving the classic-arcade
roster from Level 4 onward. The organising principle is **variety of movement
and attack styles between adjacent levels**, and **every wave that includes a
player-targeting archetype also contains at least one non-player-targeting
kind**.

Proposed ordering (open to refinement during implementation, but the
style-variety and pairing invariants are the requirement):

| Lvl | Name | Movement style | Attack style | Classic showcase / pairing |
|-----|------|----------------|--------------|-----------------------------|
| 1 | Entry | V-formation drift | none (no fire) | existing onboarding |
| 2 | Descent | Diver/swarm drift | none (no fire) | existing onboarding |
| 3 | The Core | Rect + V pairs | none (no fire) | existing onboarding |
| 4 | Firestorm | Mixed drift | aimed/spread/radial | existing fire introduction |
| 5 | Predictable Death | Fixed orbital paths | radial (memorisable) | existing Phaser |
| 6 | Invasion | **Stepping march** | aimed + tractor pull | `march` + `capturer` (targeter) |
| 7 | Segmented Assault | **Winding chain + pursuit** | radial + none | `centipede` + ghosts (targeter) |
| 8 | Gridlock | **Lanes + homing + patrol/dive** | none + aimed | `lane-traffic` + `grunt` (targeter) + `raider` (targeter) |
| 9 | Orbital Siege | **Telegraphed arcs + orbitals + pursuit** | detonation burst + radial | `orbital-strike` + `phaser` + ghosts (targeter) |
| 10 | The Gauntlet | **Dense mixed finale** | full mix | all remaining roster; every wave mixes targeters with non-targeters |

**Player-targeting archetypes** (assumption, to confirm in review):
`capturer` (tractor-beam pull), `ghost-chase/ambush/flank` (steering pursuit),
`grunt` (homing horde), `raider` (committed dive). Non-targeting kinds provide
the required counterweight in every such wave.

**Authoring mode (mixture of static + dynamic):** each new archetype's
debut/featured wave is authored as a static `fixed` wave (guaranteeing the
showcase), while the remaining waves in Levels 6–10 may be `dynamic` (seeded
per-run regeneration from their curve) so repeat runs vary. Static `fixed`
waves with no counterpart fall back to `curve` safely (existing behaviour).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Campaign size** — The campaign defines exactly **10 regular levels plus
   the boss**; `WaveManager.levelCount === 10`, the boss triggers only after the
   final wave of Level 10 clears, and the HUD renders `Level N of 10`.
2. **Roster coverage** — Every one of the eight sprint archetypes
   (`march`, `capturer`, `ghost-*`, `centipede`, `grunt`, `raider`,
   `orbital-strike`, `lane-traffic`) appears at least once in the campaign,
   verified by an automated test over the merged campaign.
3. **Player-targeter pairing** — Every wave containing a player-targeting
   archetype (`capturer`, `ghost-*`, `grunt`, `raider`) also contains at least
   one non-player-targeting kind; enforced by an automated invariant test.
4. **Style variety** — Adjacent levels differ in dominant movement/attack
   style; the mapping is documented and an automated test asserts no two
   adjacent levels share the same style profile.
5. **Onboarding preserved & authoring mix** — Levels 1–3 remain
   `shootEnabled: false` and Levels 4–10 fire; the campaign uses **both**
   `fixed` and `dynamic` waves, with every featured showcase wave `fixed` so the
   new archetype is guaranteed present for a given run seed.
6. **Difficulty continuity** — The 10-level difficulty curve is non-decreasing
   and Level 10's final target exceeds the previous campaign's final target;
   the Harvester level range is extended to the new hardest levels.
7. **Gym↔game parity & quality** — New waves reuse the shared spawners/entities
   and honour the repo-wide duplicate-body guard; all existing gym scenes still
   pass; full project test suite passes with the new changes; all related
   documentation (GDD, README, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`,
   `docs/CLASSIC_ENEMY_RESEARCH.md`) is updated. (CHANGELOG excluded — managed
   by the ship release pipeline.)

## Constraints

- No divergent copies: gameplay must run the same code in gyms and the game
  (repo-wide duplicate-body guard in `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`).
- Levels 1–3 must stay no-fire (GDD §2.4); `FIRST_FIRING_LEVEL = 4`.
- `dynamic` waves may only draw archetypes the runtime auto-sequencer supports
  as wave groups; spawner-gated archetypes (`ghosts`, `centipede`, `horde`,
  `laneTraffic`) must be delivered via their per-wave opt-in flags on `fixed`
  waves. Featured archetypes must remain present regardless of seed.
- No unplayable campaign or crash on any fallback path
  (`sequencedLevels` safety contract).
- UK English in all written output.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/waves/Formations.ts` — extend `LEVELS` to 10 level definitions with the
  new waves/opt-in flags; update the module doc-comment mapping.
- `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` — add rows for Levels 6–10 and mark featured
  waves `fixed`, chosen waves `dynamic`.
- `src/core/configStore.ts` — extend `defaultDifficultyCurves()` /
  `DEFAULT_FIXED_LEVELS` / `DEFAULT_TARGET_OVERRIDES` for Levels 6–10.
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — verify no changes needed (append/merge path);
  add coverage if new curation is required.
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — doc-comment updates ("Level 5" → final level);
  verify boss trigger via `isFinalLevel`.
- `src/waves/HarvesterSpawner.ts` — extend `HARVESTER_MAX_LEVEL` to the new
  hardest levels.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — HUD label comment/`of 10`; verify boss entry.
- `src/waves/Formations.test.ts`, `src/waves/WaveManager.test.ts`,
  `src/waves/sequencedLevels.test.ts`, `src/waves/enemyDifficulty.campaign.test.ts`
  — update level-count/level-number assertions; add coverage and diversity tests.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `README.md`,
  `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, `docs/CLASSIC_ENEMY_RESEARCH.md` —
  document the 10-level campaign and the pairing/variety rules.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** player-targeting archetypes are `capturer`, `ghost-*`,
  `grunt`, `raider`. Mitigation: confirm in review; the pairing invariant is
  parameterised by this set so it is easy to extend.
- **Risk — existing-test churn:** several tests hard-code `LEVEL_COUNT === 5`,
  "Level 5 fewer enemies" and Level 4 ≤ Level 5. Mitigation: update them as part
  of the change and keep the difficulty ramp assertions meaningful.
- **Risk — spawner-gated archetypes cannot be `dynamic` candidates.**
  Mitigation: deliver them on `fixed` waves via the existing opt-in flags.
- **Risk — difficulty spike / boss reached overpowered.** Mitigation: keep the
  curve non-decreasing and tune `targetDifficulty` for Levels 6–10.
- **Risk — scope creep** into power-up/weapon roster work
  (AH-0MV14SO0G0095IJ4). Mitigation: record as separate linked work, not in
  scope here.
- **Risk — endogenous hazards and wave completion:** `lane-traffic` and
  `orbital-strike` are non-blocking hazards and must not gate wave clear
  (existing accounting contract).

## Related work

- New enemies from classic arcade games — **AH-0MUYAQ6YH0010G52** (completed,
  parent of the eight archetype deliveries below).
- Documentation integration for the classic arcade roster —
  **AH-0MV01ER86000DNRF** (completed).
- Research catalogue and engine-constraint validation —
  **AH-0MV01EBUR003BDNK** (completed) → `docs/CLASSIC_ENEMY_RESEARCH.md`.
- Per-archetype deliveries: `march` AH-0MV01EDZS0005R20, `capturer`
  AH-0MV01EFII008298D, ghosts AH-0MV01EH2U008XT3Q, centipede
  AH-0MV01EJ92008ZZ86, grunt AH-0MV01EKTL001NRE6, raider AH-0MV01EM7U0033W7L,
  orbital-strike AH-0MV01ENX00055CG1, lane-traffic AH-0MV01EPM40008N8T.
- Per-wave generation modes (curve/fixed/dynamic) — **AH-0MUJSUQD8003FSUT**.
- Support mixed generated and scripted levels in a campaign —
  **AH-0MUH7Q6HN0006QPD**.
- Implement WaveManager — wave and level progression —
  **AH-0MU72ZK3P006CH9G**.
- Show level/wave progress as 'Level N of 5' — **AH-0MU7JTEY3004EXR2**.
- Difficulty-curve config, codec and CSV loader — **AH-0MUITRZZE000OYQE**.
- Docs: `docs/CLASSIC_ENEMY_RESEARCH.md`,
  `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md`
  (§3.2, §4.1, §2.4–2.5).
- Harvester documentation updates — **AH-0MUJRW0U6007PMB2** (completed);
  relevant because `HARVESTER_MAX_LEVEL` must be re-ranged for the longer
  campaign.

### Related work (automated report)

- **AH-0MUJRW0U6007PMB2** – Harvester documentation updates (completed).
- Repository file matches: `README.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md`,
  `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`.
- Full untruncated report: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-AH-0MV29SBAQ000HQR2.md`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 — Campaign placement: append (a), replace/re-number (b), or separate mode
  (c)? — **Answer (operator): (b)** "the key is variety of movement and attack
  styles between levels". Source: interactive reply.
- Q2 — Authoring mode: static `fixed` (a), `curve` (b), `dynamic` (c)? —
  **Answer (operator): a mixture of (a) and (c)** — hand-authored static waves
  plus seeded `dynamic` regeneration. Source: interactive reply.
- Q3 — Player-targeter pairing/progression: progressive showcase (a), dense
  from the start (b), one archetype per level (c)? — **Answer (operator): (a)**
  progressive showcase with targeters paired with other kinds. Source:
  interactive reply.
- Q4 — Total campaign length after interleaving? — **Answer (operator): (a)**
  10 levels + boss; ordering is the agent's responsibility and existing levels
  may be redesigned. Source: interactive reply.
- Q5 — No-fire onboarding: keep Levels 1–3 no-fire and interleave showcase from
  Level 4 (a), add non-firing targeters early (b), drop onboarding (c)? —
  **Answer (operator): (a)**. Source: interactive reply.
- Q6 (assumption, not asked) — Player-targeting set is `capturer`, `ghost-*`,
  `grunt`, `raider`. Evidence: `docs/CLASSIC_ENEMY_RESEARCH.md` §3 (ghosts
  steer at the live player), §5 (grunts homing-steer), §6 (raiders dive at the
  player), §2 (capturers pull the player). OPEN QUESTION for review if the set
  should differ.

# Reverse behaviour test harness and baseline — implementation plan

**Parent:** AH-0MV1J0OHP0072XA5 (Bot to use the reverse thrusters)
**Order:** 1 of 7 (test-first)
**Priority:** high · **Issue type:** task

## User story

As the demo-bot maintainer, I want deterministic tests that pin the new
reverse-thrust behaviour *before* it is implemented (TDD), so that every
reverse path is verified and no forward-model regression slips in.

## Context

The bot currently never emits reverse (`toAsteroidsInput()` hard-sets
`reverse: false`). The parent item introduces a first-class forward/reverse
thrust direction. This slice defines the failing-first verification surface
that the later slices make green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `src/ai/botHumanLike.test.ts` gains tests asserting `toAsteroidsInput()`
  emits `reverse: true` when the committed intent requests it and the ship's
  reverse thruster is enabled, and `reverse: false` on every input when the
  enable flag is off.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.test.ts` gains unit tests for the
  heading-aware forward/reverse selection, including the threshold boundary
  and a no-oscillation check across consecutive ticks.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/behaviours.test.ts` gains a test for the
  aim-preserving retreat (kiting) reverse path.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/competentBot.integration.test.ts` gains a
  deterministic target-behind scenario that asserts the bot reverses and
  reaches the target with fewer/no 180-degree turns.
- All added tests run under the existing seeded/deterministic harness (no wall

# Reverse intent and enable-flag plumbing — implementation plan

**Parent:** AH-0MV1J0OHP0072XA5 (Bot to use the reverse thrusters)
**Order:** 2 of 7
**Priority:** high · **Issue type:** feature

## User story

As a designer, I want the bot's steering intent and actuator to carry a
forward/reverse thrust direction that honours the ship's reverse-thruster
enable flag, so the bot uses exactly the thrusters the player configured.

## Context

`BotSteeringIntent` (botDecision.ts) and `SteeredIntent` (botHumanLike.ts)
have no reverse field; `toAsteroidsInput()` always emits `reverse: false`.
`PlayScene` builds the brain once and does not pass `ShipConfig`, so the
reverse-enable flag is not currently available to the bot. This slice adds the
plumbing and replaces the AH-0MV13LZ08008DN3E `reverse: false` guarantee.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `BotSteeringIntent` and `SteeredIntent` carry a `reverse: boolean` field
  that defaults to `false` when omitted, preserving existing callers.
- The ship's `asteroidsReverseEnabled` flag is surfaced from the `Player`
  source through `buildBotSnapshot()` and the derived `BotWorld` so the
  decision layer can read it each tick.
- `toAsteroidsInput()` emits `reverse: true` only when the committed intent
  requests it *and* the ship's reverse thruster is enabled; when disabled it
  emits `reverse: false` on every input and behaves exactly as today.
- The explicit `reverse: false` guarantee asserted by the
  AH-0MV13LZ08008DN3E guard test is replaced by the new contract, and the
  module doc in `botHumanLike.ts` is updated accordingly.
- `PlayScene` passes the ship's reverse-enable flag into the governor/brain
  context without changing its once-built brain lifecycle.

  `BotSteeringIntent` (plus the `buildIntent`/`idleIntent` constructors).

  `getMovementConfig()`) and carry it through `BotPlayerSource` ->
  `BotSnapshot.reverseEnabled` -> `BotWorld.reverseEnabled`.

  actuator's `reverse` output on it (intent AND flag, defence in depth).

**Parent:** AH-0MV1J0OHP0072XA5 (Bot to use the reverse thrusters)

## User story

As a player watching the demo, the bot brakes with retro-thrust instead of
overshooting a mineral, so the demo looks skilled.

The forward model currently only coasts on friction (`mayThrust()` in
`src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts`). Reverse can decelerate faster when
the nose is aligned with the travel bearing and the stopping distance exceeds
the remaining gap (parent AC1).

  (near) aligned with the desired travel bearing and the predicted stopping
  distance exceeds the remaining gap, the bot's intent requests reverse to
  decelerate.

  friction-only forward model in the covered scenarios (deterministic
  final-distance assertion).
- The reverse-braking decision is exposed as a tunable predicate alongside
  `mayThrust()` and never fires when reverse is disabled.

  compares predicted stopping distance (using reverse deceleration) with the
  remaining gap when aligned.

  `tunables.ts`.
- Have `collect`/`engage` (and `evade` where aligned) request reverse when
  the predicate holds, via `planSteering`/`buildIntent`.

# Heading-aware thrust direction — implementation plan

**Parent:** AH-0MV1J0OHP0072XA5 (Bot to use the reverse thrusters)
**Order:** 4 of 7
**Priority:** high · **Issue type:** feature

## User story

As a player watching the demo, the bot reverses toward a target behind it
instead of spinning 180 degrees, so the ship flies like a competent human.

## Context

`toAsteroidsInput()` currently always turns toward the desired bearing and
thrusts forward. When the desired bearing is behind the ship (heading error
beyond a threshold) reverse thrust is the more human response (parent AC2),
but the choice must be stable across ticks.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When the desired travel bearing is behind the ship by more than a
  configured heading-error threshold, the intent selects reverse thrust
  toward it instead of always turning 180 degrees to face it.
- Forward/reverse selection is stable across ticks: a hysteresis/dead-band
  prevents oscillation around the threshold (deterministic multi-tick test).
- When reverse is disabled, the bot falls back to the existing
  turn-180-and-thrust-forward behaviour.

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend `toAsteroidsInput()`/the governor to choose reverse when the
  absolute heading error exceeds the threshold, with an entry/exit hysteresis
  band to avoid chatter.
- Add the heading-error threshold and hysteresis tunables to `tunables.ts`.
- Keep the existing alignment-tolerance forward-thrust path unchanged.
- Update the module doc and add the boundary/no-oscillation tests (slice 1).

- `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts`
- `src/ai/botHumanLike.ts`
- `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts`
- `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.test.ts`

As a player watching the bot retreat from a threat with its nose still on the

# Bug: `npm run record` fails with 'Unknown argument: /usr/bin/node'

**Discovered while trying to view the action-intensity telemetry** produced by AH-0MUZMTTYH008KVS2. The dev session recorder delivered by AH-0MUY08W7Y004GATZ is completely broken as a CLI — every invocation fails before doing any work.

```text
$ npm run record -- --auto --bot --seed 12345
Unknown argument: /usr/bin/node
```

## Steps to reproduce

```bash
npm run record -- --auto --bot --seed 12345
# or even:
node scripts/record-session.mjs --help
```

Both fail with `Unknown argument: /usr/bin/node`.

## Root cause

`scripts/record-session.mjs` (lines 277-278):

```js
if (process.argv[1] && fileURLToPath(import.meta.url) === process.argv[1]) {
  main(process.argv).then(...)
```

`main()` is passed the **full** `process.argv` (`[nodePath, scriptPath, ...flags]`), but `parseRecordArgs(argv)` expects only the flag list — its default `process.argv.slice(2)` is bypassed because an argument is supplied. The parser therefore treats `process.argv[0]` (`/usr/bin/node`) as an unknown flag and throws.

Note the sibling tool `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` does not have this bug: it calls `main()` with no argv and slices internally.

## Expected behaviour

`npm run record -- <flags>` starts the Vite dev server with telemetry enabled, drives the browser, and writes `recordings/session-<seed>-<ts>.jsonl`. `--help` prints usage.

## Suggested fix (one line)

Pass the sliced argv in the entry guard:

```js
main(process.argv.slice(2)).then(...)
```

(equivalently, call `main()` with no argument so the `parseRecordArgs` default applies).

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1** — `npm run record -- --help` prints usage and exits 0 (no 'Unknown argument' error).
- **AC2** — `npm run record -- --auto --bot --seed <N>` runs to completion and writes a JSONL recording to `recordings/`.
- **AC3** — A regression test covers `parseRecordArgs`/entry-point argument handling so the full-argv mistake cannot recur.

## Related

- `discovered-from:AH-0MUZMTTYH008KVS2` (action-intensity telemetry, epic).
- Owning deliverable: AH-0MUY08W7Y004GATZ (dev recording/analysis/replay tooling).
- Blocking observation of the action-intensity metric via the ready-made recorder.
